extraction.body: Apple today announced a new high-end MacBook Pro , which is available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes. The new device has a PROLED XDR display that supports touch gestures, and a glowing rear Apple logo. Pricing on the ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model. Apple says the ‌MacBook Pro‌ has the "world's best display in a pro laptop." The PROLED display uses tandem OLED paired with advanced algorithms in the display engine and factory calibration for "exceptional brightness, striking contrast, and vivid true-to-life colors." The display offers up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, along with a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. A display engine controls the color and luminance of each pixel, compensating for content, temperature, environment, and pixel use. ProMotion technology is available with refresh rates ranging from 10Hz to 120Hz. An antireflective coating cuts down on glare in bright lighting conditions, and there is an option to order the new ‌MacBook Pro‌ with a nano-texture display. A touch sensor is built directly in the display panel, so there is no added latency. Apple says touch interactions feel "incredibly responsive and refined." Users can scroll through a webpage with a swipe, pinch to zoom in on a photo, drag and drop slides from one presentation to another, and double-tap a window to have it fill the screen. A new hinge design offers more stability when using touch, and advanced video stabilization smooths the camera feed when using touch on a video call. Apple says macOS automatically translates touch into clicks, so many existing apps will work with touch right away. The ‌MacBook Pro‌ is up to 1mm slimmer than the existing version, and it is lighter weight at just three pounds for the 14-inch model and four pounds for the 16-inch model. There is no more notch, with Apple instead adding a small Dynamic Island that takes up less space. The ‌Dynamic Island‌ houses Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. Like on the iPhone, it offers a quick way to see and interact with important information. Smaller bezels mean the 16-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ display is now 16.3 inches in size, while the 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ is now 14.2 inches. The new ‌MacBook Pro‌ uses the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the ‌MacBook Pro‌ models announced back in March, but there is a redesigned thermal architecture that directs warm air away from the display. There is support for up to 128GB of unified memory, and a new six-speaker sound system with 50 percent deeper bass. There are three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe , and a headphone jack. The new machines support up to four external displays and come with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Fast charging allows the ‌MacBook Pro‌ to be charged to 50 percent in 30 minutes, and up to 16TB storage is available. Apple is selling the ‌OLED‌ ‌MacBook Pro‌ models alongside the existing mini-LED models and the new M6 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌. Pre-orders are available now, with a launch coming on Friday, November 6. coreStoryFacts.text: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display, its first touchscreen laptop.
While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years.
Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:
The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices.
You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design.
The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support.
We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6.
The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser .
Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.
Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar?
It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it.
Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook.
Apple’s Mac lineup consists of MacBook, MacBoo…
The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos.
Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users.

In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd
I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction.

extraction.body: Apple has officially introduced the all-new MacBook Pro, marking a major milestone as the company's first touchscreen Mac. Powered by the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, this high-end laptop features a completely redesigned, thinner, and lighter form factor alongside cutting-edge display technology. The headline feature is the PROLED XDR display, which replaces previous Mini-LED panels with tandem OLED technology. This upgrade increases peak HDR brightness to 2000 nits and introduces intuitive touch capabilities to the macOS ecosystem for the first time. The physical design also revives the classic light-up Apple logo on the exterior lid. The 14-inch model weighs 3 pounds with dimensions of 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inches, while the 16-inch model weighs 4 pounds with dimensions of 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches. Biometric security continues to rely on Touch ID, as Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity are not included in this release. Available in silver and space black, finishes can be paired with standard or nano-texture display options. Pre-orders are open immediately, with official deliveries scheduled to begin on November 6.

extraction.body: Apple today announced a new high-end MacBook Pro , which is available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes. The new device has a PROLED XDR display that supports touch gestures, and a glowing rear Apple logo. Pricing on the ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model. Apple says the ‌MacBook Pro‌ has the "world's best display in a pro laptop." The PROLED display uses tandem OLED paired with advanced algorithms in the display engine and factory calibration for "exceptional brightness, striking contrast, and vivid true-to-life colors." The display offers up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, along with a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. A display engine controls the color and luminance of each pixel, compensating for content, temperature, environment, and pixel use. ProMotion technology is available with refresh rates ranging from 10Hz to 120Hz. An antireflective coating cuts down on glare in bright lighting conditions, and there is an option to order the new ‌MacBook Pro‌ with a nano-texture display. A touch sensor is built directly in the display panel, so there is no added latency. Apple says touch interactions feel "incredibly responsive and refined." Users can scroll through a webpage with a swipe, pinch to zoom in on a photo, drag and drop slides from one presentation to another, and double-tap a window to have it fill the screen. A new hinge design offers more stability when using touch, and advanced video stabilization smooths the camera feed when using touch on a video call. Apple says macOS automatically translates touch into clicks, so many existing apps will work with touch right away. The ‌MacBook Pro‌ is up to 1mm slimmer than the existing version, and it is lighter weight at just three pounds for the 14-inch model and four pounds for the 16-inch model. There is no more notch, with Apple instead adding a small Dynamic Island that takes up less space. The ‌Dynamic Island‌ houses Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. Like on the iPhone, it offers a quick way to see and interact with important information. Smaller bezels mean the 16-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ display is now 16.3 inches in size, while the 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ is now 14.2 inches. The new ‌MacBook Pro‌ uses the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the ‌MacBook Pro‌ models announced back in March, but there is a redesigned thermal architecture that directs warm air away from the display. There is support for up to 128GB of unified memory, and a new six-speaker sound system with 50 percent deeper bass. There are three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe , and a headphone jack. The new machines support up to four external displays and come with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Fast charging allows the ‌MacBook Pro‌ to be charged to 50 percent in 30 minutes, and up to 16TB storage is available. Apple is selling the ‌OLED‌ ‌MacBook Pro‌ models alongside the existing mini-LED models and the new M6 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌. Pre-orders are available now, with a launch coming on Friday, November 6. passages: While rumors had suggested the new mini would get an OLED display, the update packs a bigger punch than that.
But central to the refresh is indeed a larger 8.5-inch OLED Super Retina XDR screen.
That’s 0.2 inches larger than the previous generation’s Liquid Retina display, made possible by Apple's design team shrinking the bezels by 24% all around while keeping the same overall dimensions.
If you’re upgrading from an older iPad mini or iPad, you can expect a more noticeable leap in everyday performance, from opening apps and handling daily tasks to exporting files.
For those coming from the A17 Pro, Apple promises up to 60% faster multithreaded CPU performance, 4.5x faster AI performance, and 2.7x better graphics performance generation over generation.
Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread are all supported here, courtesy of the Apple-made N1 chip.

Ahead of its Pro and Tell experience on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 — and precisely two years and three days since it last introduced a mini tablet, the iPad mini 8.3-inch (2024) — Apple has just unveiled the eighth-generation iPad mini, starting at $699 / £699 / AU$1,099.
Now, if you were hoping for a range of color options, Apple is slimming things down to just two.
The new iPad mini comes in Starlight or Midnight, so it’s a fond farewell to Blue, Purple, and Space Gray.
All of this should come together to make for an excellent experience on iPadOS 27, with full Siri AI compatibility thrown in for good measure.
For those wondering, the iPhone Duo measures the same 5.33mm when unfolded, so the Duo and mini are equal here.
Tweeters for better high-end audio are also inserted between the aluminum and glass.
This new display is, however, still locked to 60Hz, so the iPad Pro remains Apple's only 120Hz-compatible iPad.
With audio improvements, a slimmer build, and a Nano-Texture display option, it feels like we're inching closer to an iPad Mini Pro.
I also think the dust and water resistance upgrade will be a huge hit with families, and kids generally like the mini's smaller size.
As for accessories, it’ll still support the Apple Pencil Pro or the Apple Pencil USB-C, and Apple is shipping a new TechWoven Folio Case in navy blue and taupe.
There’s still no official Apple Magic Keyboard, but we’ll no doubt see some third-party options.

The display grows to 8.5 inches while keeping the same physical dimensions as the previous generation, achieved through 24 percent thinner bezels.
The Super Retina XDR OLED panel delivers deep pixel-level blacks, a 2,000,000 to 1 contrast ratio, and a peak brightness reaching up to 1200 nits.
For outdoor productivity, Apple is also introducing an optional nano-texture glass finish that drastically cuts reflections in challenging ambient light.
Under the hood, the tablet is powered by the high-performance A20 Pro chip featuring integrated Neural Accelerators within each GPU core.
The processor delivers a 30 percent boost in CPU tasks alongside a 50 percent leap in graphics performance for demanding 3D games and animation tools.
Working alongside a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, the A20 Pro powers next-generation Apple Intelligence features and conversational Siri AI throughout iPadOS 27.

The tablet also incorporates Acoustic Display technology, projecting stereo audio directly forward from the panel for rich media immersion.

Creative workflows gain a major boost with full support for Apple Pencil Pro, enabling squeeze gestures, barrel roll rotation, and haptic feedback.
Connectivity is brought up to speed with Wi-Fi 7 support, upgraded 5G cellular with eSIM, and a faster 10Gbps USB-C port with fast charging.
Apple has also developed a new two-panel TechWoven Smart Folio in navy blue and taupe that magnetically attaches for adjustable viewing angles.
In Canada, the new iPad mini starts at 949 Canadian dollars for the Wi-Fi variant and 1,149 Canadian dollars for the Wi-Fi plus Cellular configuration.
Canadian pre-orders kick off on Wednesday, October 28, with retail deliveries and in-store availability starting Friday, November 6, 2026.

coreStoryFacts.text: While rumors had suggested the new mini would get an OLED display, the update packs a bigger punch than that.
But central to the refresh is indeed a larger 8.5-inch OLED Super Retina XDR screen.
That’s 0.2 inches larger than the previous generation’s Liquid Retina display, made possible by Apple's design team shrinking the bezels by 24% all around while keeping the same overall dimensions.
If you’re upgrading from an older iPad mini or iPad, you can expect a more noticeable leap in everyday performance, from opening apps and handling daily tasks to exporting files.
For those coming from the A17 Pro, Apple promises up to 60% faster multithreaded CPU performance, 4.5x faster AI performance, and 2.7x better graphics performance generation over generation.
Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread are all supported here, courtesy of the Apple-made N1 chip.

Ahead of its Pro and Tell experience on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 — and precisely two years and three days since it last introduced a mini tablet, the iPad mini 8.3-inch (2024) — Apple has just unveiled the eighth-generation iPad mini, starting at $699 / £699 / AU$1,099.
Now, if you were hoping for a range of color options, Apple is slimming things down to just two.
The new iPad mini comes in Starlight or Midnight, so it’s a fond farewell to Blue, Purple, and Space Gray.
All of this should come together to make for an excellent experience on iPadOS 27, with full Siri AI compatibility thrown in for good measure.
For those wondering, the iPhone Duo measures the same 5.33mm when unfolded, so the Duo and mini are equal here.
Tweeters for better high-end audio are also inserted between the aluminum and glass.
This new display is, however, still locked to 60Hz, so the iPad Pro remains Apple's only 120Hz-compatible iPad.
With audio improvements, a slimmer build, and a Nano-Texture display option, it feels like we're inching closer to an iPad Mini Pro.
I also think the dust and water resistance upgrade will be a huge hit with families, and kids generally like the mini's smaller size.
As for accessories, it’ll still support the Apple Pencil Pro or the Apple Pencil USB-C, and Apple is shipping a new TechWoven Folio Case in navy blue and taupe.
There’s still no official Apple Magic Keyboard, but we’ll no doubt see some third-party options.

If you’ve been holding out hope for a new iPad mini, you could say Apple has answered the call. Ahead of its Pro and Tell experience on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 — and precisely two years and three days since it last introduced a mini tablet, the iPad mini 8.3-inch (2024) — Apple has just unveiled the eighth-generation iPad mini, starting at $699 / £699 / AU$1,099. While rumors had suggested the new mini would get an OLED display, the update packs a bigger punch than that. But central to the refresh is indeed a larger 8.5-inch OLED Super Retina XDR screen. That’s 0.2 inches larger than the previous generation’s Liquid Retina display, made possible by Apple's design team shrinking the bezels by 24% all around while keeping the same overall dimensions. The Super Retina XDR display is a welcome addition, promising a more immersive view with more vibrant, crisper visuals. And since the iPad mini is often touted as a device to carry around — and is even used in cockpits by pilots — it also gets a brightness boost, now topping out at 1,200 nits, which is a considerable leap over the previous mini's 500 nits. The screen still supports the P3 color gamut and Apple’s True Tone technology, which matches the display’s color temperature to your surroundings. This new display is, however, still locked to 60Hz, so the iPad Pro remains Apple's only 120Hz-compatible iPad. Under and around the iPad mini's OLED screen is a new ‘Acoustic Display’ that places custom-designed woofers in the screen for higher peak volume and stronger bass. Tweeters for better high-end audio are also inserted between the aluminum and glass. I’m eager to test this new audio system out, but it’s no doubt an improvement over the previous mini's stereo speakers. Trickling down from the iPad Pro is a Nano-Texture display option. Similar to the screen technology used on the iPhone Duo — and even the iMac , MacBook Pro, and aforementioned iPad Pro — this layer can help block natural and artificial reflections. I use it daily on a 14-inch MacBook Pro, and with that brightness boost, it'll make the new iPad mini more of a road warrior, even in harsher lighting. You'll need to opt for at least the 256GB model to add Nano Texture, though, and it's a $100 feature, bringing the iPad mini's price from $799 to $899. The tablet still starts at 128GB, which is a tad disappointing. A big surprise addition is that the new mini's aluminum design adds IP67 water and dust resistance, making it more durable on the go and potentially a better option as a kids' tablet. The iPad mini is also thinner and lighter than its predecessor, measuring 5.33mm thick and weighing 254g, compared to 6.35mm and 295g, respectively. For those wondering, the iPhone Duo measures the same 5.33mm when unfolded, so the Duo and mini are equal here. Now, if you were hoping for a range of color options, Apple is slimming things down to just two. The new iPad mini comes in Starlight or Midnight, so it’s a fond farewell to Blue, Purple, and Space Gray. Under the hood, the eighth-generation iPad mini gets a sizable leap to Apple’s 2nm A20 Pro chip, but which chip edition you get depends on your storage configuration. The 128GB and 256GB models feature a five-core CPU (two super cores and three efficiency cores), a seven-core GPU, and a 16-core Neural Engine. The 512GB variant offers a more capable six-core CPU (two super cores and four efficiency cores), the same seven-core GPU, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. If you’re upgrading from an older iPad mini or iPad, you can expect a more noticeable leap in everyday performance, from opening apps and handling daily tasks to exporting files. For those coming from the A17 Pro, Apple promises up to 60% faster multithreaded CPU performance, 4.5x faster AI performance, and 2.7x better graphics performance generation over generation. Apple hasn’t yet confirmed the amount of memory inside the new iPad mini (we may need to wait for reviews or a teardown), but like the latest-generation iPhones, unified memory bandwidth has doubled. All of this should come together to make for an excellent experience on iPadOS 27, with full Siri AI compatibility thrown in for good measure. And remember, the iPad mini supports the full multitasking experience iPad offers. Compared to the iPhone Duo, you can do more than just split the screen, which makes a big difference. Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread are all supported here, courtesy of the Apple-made N1 chip. If you opt for a cellular iPad mini, the C2 modem enables cellular connectivity. Apple promises it can deliver up to 50% faster data speeds compared to the previous modem in the seventh-generation iPad mini. Lastly, the 12MP Center Stage camera remains embedded in the now-slimmer bezels around the 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR display. It still sits on the longer side of the iPad mini, like the rest of the lineup, and is joined on the rear by a 12MP camera and Adaptive True Tone flash. Now, Apple has delivered solid updates across the board — a better screen, a new audio system for richer sound, a sizable performance leap, and perhaps the biggest sleeper surprise: IP67 water and dust resistance. These upgrades do come at a higher price, though: the new iPad mini starts at $699 / £699 / AU$1,099 for Wi-Fi or $849 / £849 / AU$1,349 for Wi-Fi and Cellular. That’s a leap over the previous 7th Gen iPad mini, which started at $499 / £499 / AU$799 at launch, then jumped to $599 / £599 / AU$949 in June this year. Even so, you get a much better-equipped processor for smooth performance in the near term and the long term, paired with a display that'll be a big jump on its own, no matter what generation you come from. With audio improvements, a slimmer build, and a Nano-Texture display option, it feels like we're inching closer to an iPad Mini Pro. I also think the dust and water resistance upgrade will be a huge hit with families, and kids generally like the mini's smaller size. Apple will begin taking orders for the iPad mini on October 28, 2026 — this Wednesday, if you’re counting down the days — at 10:10am PT / 1:10pm ET / 5:10pm GMT, and it will begin shipping on November 6, 2026. It’s likely that the iPad mini could be joined by a few other devices on that launch date, but for now, it sits between the HomePod mini 2 , which arrives on October 30, 2026, and the HomeView or Apple TV 4K , which lands on November 13, 2026. I can’t wait to get my hands on the new iPad mini and see how it performs, especially compared to the previous generation, and it's small enough to go wherever I go. As for accessories, it’ll still support the Apple Pencil Pro or the Apple Pencil USB-C, and Apple is shipping a new TechWoven Folio Case in navy blue and taupe. There’s still no official Apple Magic Keyboard, but we’ll no doubt see some third-party options. I’m keen to know what you think about Apple’s upgrade this time around with the iPad mini, so sound off in the comments below. extraction.body: The newest iPad mini features has an OLED display and an updated design that’s thinner and lighter. Days ago, Apple announced a new iPad mini . And at Apple’s “Pro and Tell” event, I had the chance to play around with it for a little while. The first thing that struck me was how thin it is. Apple says it’s just 5.4mm thick , which means it’s 0.9mm or around 14% slimmer than the last-generation iPad mini. It’s definitely noticeable. It weighs a little less too. On the whole, I thought it felt nicer in the hands. The display is now OLED. I didn’t notice a huge difference, but it does look very nice. At 8.5 inches , it’s a bit bigger too, but again, I can’t say I noticed the size difference. Despite the larger display, the overall size of the iPad mini is mostly the same; that’s because Apple shrunk the bezels as opposed to making the iPad mini larger overall. I think that’s the right decision. The iPad mini has always been loved for its compact size. For the first time, the iPad mini can be ordered with a display that has a nano-texture finish. This greatly reduces glare and reflection, and would be my choice if I were ordering the new iPad mini. However, it’s worth noting that it’s only available on the 256GB and 512GB models, and it costs an extra S$150. The display is 8.5 inches now, but I didn’t really notice the size difference. Performance is brisk, as you would expect from a tablet sporting Apple’s newest A20 Pro chip. However, the display is limited to 60Hz , so it doesn’t look or feel as fluid as, say, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. The iPad mini has a new speaker system too, with tweeters at the sides and woofers under the display. Unfortunately, given how noisy the venue was, I couldn’t hear it in action. The new iPad mini comes in two colours: Midnight and Starlight. Pictured here is Starlight. Based on first impressions, this looks like a solid update for the iPad mini. The slightly larger and higher quality OLED display is a much-welcomed update, and it’s noticeably thinner and lighter. The IP67 dust and water resistance rating should make it a more hardy device that you can take with you to more places too. Stay tuned for my full review. Days ago, Apple announced a new iPad mini . And at Apple’s “Pro and Tell” event, I had the chance to play around with it for a little while.

The first thing that struck me was how thin it is. Apple says it’s just 5.4mm thick , which means it’s 0.9mm or around 14% slimmer than the last-generation iPad mini. It’s definitely noticeable. It weighs a little less too. On the whole, I thought it felt nicer in the hands.

The display is now OLED. I didn’t notice a huge difference, but it does look very nice. At 8.5 inches , it’s a bit bigger too, but again, I can’t say I noticed the size difference. I think that’s the right decision. The iPad mini has always been loved for its compact size.

sources.title: Amazon overhauls aging devices lineup with higher-priced Alexa tablet, dumping the budget Fire - CNBC
passages: Amazon on Thursday debuted a set of new, pricier Alexa tablets and said it's ditching its budget-friendly Fire lineup, marking a significant shift in the e-commerce juggernaut's devices strategy.
Amazon denied that rising memory costs played a role in its decision to charge more for the Alexa tablet.
But Panos Panay, the company's devices boss, acknowledged that the shortage made it "quite tricky" to build a premium tablet at a reasonable price without making any "trade-offs."
Alexa is front and center in the new tablets, via a "dynamic tab" on the home screen that offers recommendations and lets users quickly pick up where they left off reading or watching a TV show.
Users can say "Alexa" or tap the "Ask Alexa" button to ask questions.
The Fire lineup includes a 10-inch and 8-inch model as well as two versions targeted for kids.
The $550 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro costs more than double the price of the $155 Fire HD 10, Amazon's base model, and puts it more in line with Apple 's iPad, which runs from $449 to $1,199.
Amazon added a sleeker, sturdier aluminum backing, higher resolution display and faster processors.
The launch comes as Amazon and other device makers are grappling with a historic surge in memory prices .
Amazon in August boosted prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs and other hardware, citing the memory crunch.
In a demo, Panay showed how users could watch a TikTok clip of someone cooking on a grill and ask Alexa to shop for a burger press used in the video.
Users can also pull up a game schedule and add every date to their calendar, Amazon said.

Amazon has historically sold its devices at or near the cost of manufacturing them, partly to undercut competitors with extremely cheap prices, but also with the goal of promoting its other products and services.
It's hoped that for every $80 Echo smart speaker it sells, users will purchase movies, audiobook subscriptions or items from its sprawling webstore, which tend to have higher margins.
The company has recently taken steps to make more money from its devices business under CEO Andy Jassy , who succeeded founder Jeff Bezos in 2021.
Last year, it introduced pricier versions of its Echo smart speakers and began charging non-Prime members a subscription for Alexa+ , the souped-up version of its digital assistant.
"I think the team did a good job designing without making that trade," Panay told CNBC in an interview.
"They gave you the full craftsmanship of a product, but are able to keep it at that price point."

sources.title: Amazon unveils new Echo devices, powered by its AI, Alexa+ - TechCrunch
passages: To showcase the AI’s capabilities, Amazon is releasing four new Echo devices with improved processing power and memory: the Echo Dot Max, Echo Studio, Echo Show 8, and Echo Show 11.

At its annual hardware event, Amazon introduced a new lineup of Echo devices, built specifically for its AI assistant, Alexa+, which has already rolled out to millions of customers through its early access program.
This will later include an Alexa+ Store, where users can explore services from brands like Fandango, GrubHub, Lyft, Priceline, Taskrabbit, Thumbtack, and Yahoo Sports.
The devices will also be able to manage new or existing subscriptions with Amazon’s own services like Amazon Music, Amazon Kids+, or Alexa Emergency Assist and customize their Alexa experience.

With this feature, the devices allow Alexa to act on events happening in the home, like delivering a reminder when a particular person walks in the room or alerting you to an open garage door before you go to bed at night.
Plus, Amazon is teaming up with smart ring maker Oura to bring personalized health and wellness suggestions to Alexa devices.
This could help do things like add workout reminders or nudges to head to bed to get the best sleep.
The $219.99 Echo Studio, meanwhile, features a new spherical design, allowing it to be 40% smaller than the original, says Amazon.
The chip also improves detection of the wake word by over 50%, Amazon claims.

As Alexa devices with a screen, the displays also work well for accessing entertainment, like streaming audio and video, managing home organization and family activities, and managing household shopping needs.
The latter integrates with Amazon, Whole Foods, and Amazon Fresh to make reordering favorites and delivery tracking easier.

passages: Today, Amazon announced the latest generation of Alexa devices , each designed for Alexa+ and purpose-built for the moments and tasks customers turn to Alexa for most.
The next-generation Echo Dot is designed for everywhere you can imagine and packs even more into its compact form factor.

For the first time, it includes a built-in smart home hub, so Alexa connects to hundreds of compatible devices such as lights, locks, thermostats right out of the box, plus a built-in eero Wi-Fi extender that adds up to 93 square metres of coverage to your existing network.
At its core is Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon, with a new AI Accelerator built for on-device AI that sharpens conversational detection and filters out background noise.
Music, audiobooks, and podcasts sound great on the new Echo Dot, with crisp vocals and 50% more bass than its predecessor.
Echo Studio with Home Camera takes Amazon's best-sounding speaker and gives it a richer understanding of the room around it, making Alexa even more useful.
The camera enables a new Adaptive Volume feature that optimises playback as you move throughout the room.

What's new is context: with more awareness of its surroundings, Alexa can help in real time —explaining the rules on a board game box you hold up, recognizing a box of cereal to help you reorder it, or letting you check in on the room from the Alexa app while you're away.
Privacy is built into every Echo device from the ground up, and customers are in control of their experience.
There are clear visual indicators when Alexa is listening, and a dedicated privacy button turns the microphones off completely.

The new Echo Studio with Home Camera ships today for RRP A$479. For more information about the new Echo studio with Home Camera check out this page amazon.com.au/echostudiowithcamera . Echo Time is purpose-built for the bedside—with a customizable display and camera-free design to make waking up and winding down effortless. Make it yours with hundreds of clock face variations to choose from – including everything from analogue and modern to playful designs that fit any space and style. Its new sleep sensing technology, powered by Omnisense sensor fusion, can sense when you're in lighter sleep and wakes you within an optimal window ahead of your scheduled alarm. As your alarm approaches, the display gradually brightens to mimic a natural sunrise and the tone builds gently in volume to help ease you awake. Available today for RRP A$379 in Coral Pink, Glacier White, and Graphite. For more information check out this page amazon.com.au/echotime . Privacy is built into every Echo device from the ground up, and customers are in control of their experience. There are clear visual indicators when Alexa is listening, and a dedicated privacy button turns the microphones off completely. Sleep sensing capabilities can be turned on or off at any time via device settings in the Alexa app or by turning off the microphone using the mute button.

coreStoryFacts.text: Amazon on Thursday debuted a set of new, pricier Alexa tablets and said it's ditching its budget-friendly Fire lineup, marking a significant shift in the e-commerce juggernaut's devices strategy.
Amazon denied that rising memory costs played a role in its decision to charge more for the Alexa tablet.
But Panos Panay, the company's devices boss, acknowledged that the shortage made it "quite tricky" to build a premium tablet at a reasonable price without making any "trade-offs."
Alexa is front and center in the new tablets, via a "dynamic tab" on the home screen that offers recommendations and lets users quickly pick up where they left off reading or watching a TV show.
Users can say "Alexa" or tap the "Ask Alexa" button to ask questions.
The Fire lineup includes a 10-inch and 8-inch model as well as two versions targeted for kids.
The $550 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro costs more than double the price of the $155 Fire HD 10, Amazon's base model, and puts it more in line with Apple 's iPad, which runs from $449 to $1,199.
Amazon added a sleeker, sturdier aluminum backing, higher resolution display and faster processors.
The launch comes as Amazon and other device makers are grappling with a historic surge in memory prices .
Amazon in August boosted prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs and other hardware, citing the memory crunch.
In a demo, Panay showed how users could watch a TikTok clip of someone cooking on a grill and ask Alexa to shop for a burger press used in the video.
Users can also pull up a game schedule and add every date to their calendar, Amazon said.

Amazon has historically sold its devices at or near the cost of manufacturing them, partly to undercut competitors with extremely cheap prices, but also with the goal of promoting its other products and services.
It's hoped that for every $80 Echo smart speaker it sells, users will purchase movies, audiobook subscriptions or items from its sprawling webstore, which tend to have higher margins.
The company has recently taken steps to make more money from its devices business under CEO Andy Jassy , who succeeded founder Jeff Bezos in 2021.
Last year, it introduced pricier versions of its Echo smart speakers and began charging non-Prime members a subscription for Alexa+ , the souped-up version of its digital assistant.
"I think the team did a good job designing without making that trade," Panay told CNBC in an interview.
"They gave you the full craftsmanship of a product, but are able to keep it at that price point."
To showcase the AI’s capabilities, Amazon is releasing four new Echo devices with improved processing power and memory: the Echo Dot Max, Echo Studio, Echo Show 8, and Echo Show 11.

At its annual hardware event, Amazon introduced a new lineup of Echo devices, built specifically for its AI assistant, Alexa+, which has already rolled out to millions of customers through its early access program.
This will later include an Alexa+ Store, where users can explore services from brands like Fandango, GrubHub, Lyft, Priceline, Taskrabbit, Thumbtack, and Yahoo Sports.
The devices will also be able to manage new or existing subscriptions with Amazon’s own services like Amazon Music, Amazon Kids+, or Alexa Emergency Assist and customize their Alexa experience.

With this feature, the devices allow Alexa to act on events happening in the home, like delivering a reminder when a particular person walks in the room or alerting you to an open garage door before you go to bed at night.
Plus, Amazon is teaming up with smart ring maker Oura to bring personalized health and wellness suggestions to Alexa devices.

The company unveiled 8-inch, 11-inch and 12-inch models, which start at $230 and run up to $550. All devices are available for preorder on Thursday and will begin shipping Oct. 14. Amazon has historically sold its devices at or near the cost of manufacturing them, partly to undercut competitors with extremely cheap prices, but also with the goal of promoting its other products and services. The $550 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro costs more than double the price of the $155 Fire HD 10, Amazon's base model, and puts it more in line with Apple 's iPad, which runs from $449 to $1,199. The launch comes as Amazon and other device makers are grappling with a historic surge in memory prices . Amazon in August boosted prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs and other hardware, citing the memory crunch. And earlier this year, Apple raised its prices on MacBooks and iPads, while Nintendo hiked the price of its Switch 2 console. The company unveiled 8-inch, 11-inch and 12-inch models, which start at $230 and run up to $550. All devices are available for preorder on Thursday and will begin shipping Oct. 14.

Amazon has historically sold its devices at or near the cost of manufacturing them, partly to undercut competitors with extremely cheap prices, but also with the goal of promoting its other products and services. It's hoped that for every $80 Echo smart speaker it sells, users will purchase movies, audiobook subscriptions or items from its sprawling webstore, which tend to have higher margins.

The company has recently taken steps to make more money from its devices business under CEO Andy Jassy , who succeeded founder Jeff Bezos in 2021. Last year, it introduced pricier versions of its Echo smart speakers and began charging non-Prime members a subscription for Alexa+ , the souped-up version of its digital assistant.

sources.title: Amazon unveils new Echo devices, powered by its AI, Alexa+ - TechCrunch
passages: To showcase the AI’s capabilities, Amazon is releasing four new Echo devices with improved processing power and memory: the Echo Dot Max, Echo Studio, Echo Show 8, and Echo Show 11.

At its annual hardware event, Amazon introduced a new lineup of Echo devices, built specifically for its AI assistant, Alexa+, which has already rolled out to millions of customers through its early access program.
This will later include an Alexa+ Store, where users can explore services from brands like Fandango, GrubHub, Lyft, Priceline, Taskrabbit, Thumbtack, and Yahoo Sports.
The devices will also be able to manage new or existing subscriptions with Amazon’s own services like Amazon Music, Amazon Kids+, or Alexa Emergency Assist and customize their Alexa experience.

With this feature, the devices allow Alexa to act on events happening in the home, like delivering a reminder when a particular person walks in the room or alerting you to an open garage door before you go to bed at night.
Plus, Amazon is teaming up with smart ring maker Oura to bring personalized health and wellness suggestions to Alexa devices.
This could help do things like add workout reminders or nudges to head to bed to get the best sleep.
The $219.99 Echo Studio, meanwhile, features a new spherical design, allowing it to be 40% smaller than the original, says Amazon.
The chip also improves detection of the wake word by over 50%, Amazon claims.

As Alexa devices with a screen, the displays also work well for accessing entertainment, like streaming audio and video, managing home organization and family activities, and managing household shopping needs.
The latter integrates with Amazon, Whole Foods, and Amazon Fresh to make reordering favorites and delivery tracking easier.

Key to the devices are the Alexa+ integrations, allowing the speakers to respond to more queries than earlier models, offering support for natural language conversations, more complex questions, and soon, more add-ons and capabilities.

To showcase the AI’s capabilities, Amazon is releasing four new Echo devices with improved processing power and memory: the Echo Dot Max, Echo Studio, Echo Show 8, and Echo Show 11. Key to the devices are the Alexa+ integrations, allowing the speakers to respond to more queries than earlier models, offering support for natural language conversations, more complex questions, and soon, more add-ons and capabilities. This will later include an Alexa+ Store, where users can explore services from brands like Fandango, GrubHub, Lyft, Priceline, Taskrabbit, Thumbtack, and Yahoo Sports. The devices will also be able to manage new or existing subscriptions with Amazon’s own services like Amazon Music, Amazon Kids+, or Alexa Emergency Assist and customize their Alexa experience. The new Echo devices launching today run on Amazon’s custom-designed silicon chips, the AZ3 and AZ3 Pro, which include an AI Accelerator designed to run AI edge models. The AZ3 enables better conversation detection on the Echo Dot, letting people talk to the device from anywhere in the room, while still filtering out background noise. The chip also improves detection of the wake word by over 50%, Amazon claims. The other three devices — the Studio, Show 8, and 11 — use the AZ3 Pro, which adds support for advanced language models and vision transformers. Plus, the AZ3 Pro-enabled devices include Ominisense, a custom sensor platform for ambient AI that uses the 13-megapixel camera on new Echo Show devices, audio, ultrasound, Wi-Fi radar, accelerometer, and Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI). With this feature, the devices allow Alexa to act on events happening in the home, like delivering a reminder when a particular person walks in the room or alerting you to an open garage door before you go to bed at night. The new Echo Dot Max, $99.99, adds nearly three times the bass for better sound. The two-way speaker includes a woofer for the deep bass and a custom tweeter for the high notes. The $219.99 Echo Studio, meanwhile, features a new spherical design, allowing it to be 40% smaller than the original, says Amazon. The Echo Studio also includes a high-excursion woofer, spatial audio, and Dolby Atmos, and an upgraded light ring for better visual understanding of what Alexa is doing or processing. The company notes consumers can connect up to five Echo Studio or Echo Dot Max devices with compatible Fire TV sticks for an immersive sound system in their home, and it plans to sell products in Alexa Home Theater bundles. Also new are two smart displays, the Echo Show 8 ($179.99) and Echo Show 11 ($219.99), which both have a new design, improved picture quality, a 13-megapixel camera, a larger screen area, new front-facing stereo speakers, a custom woofer, and Alexa+ powered features. The AI assistant will run a new smart home experience called Alexa+ Home, which combines things like event summaries from Ring camera feeds and a smart home hub that supports Matter, Thread, and Zigbee. As Alexa devices with a screen, the displays also work well for accessing entertainment, like streaming audio and video, managing home organization and family activities, and managing household shopping needs. The latter integrates with Amazon, Whole Foods, and Amazon Fresh to make reordering favorites and delivery tracking easier. Plus, Amazon is teaming up with smart ring maker Oura to bring personalized health and wellness suggestions to Alexa devices. This could help do things like add workout reminders or nudges to head to bed to get the best sleep. Other devices from Withings and Wyze will be supported in the future. sources.title: Amazon unveils its newest lineup of Alexa+ devices - About Amazon Australia
passages: Today, Amazon announced the latest generation of Alexa devices , each designed for Alexa+ and purpose-built for the moments and tasks customers turn to Alexa for most.
The next-generation Echo Dot is designed for everywhere you can imagine and packs even more into its compact form factor.

For the first time, it includes a built-in smart home hub, so Alexa connects to hundreds of compatible devices such as lights, locks, thermostats right out of the box, plus a built-in eero Wi-Fi extender that adds up to 93 square metres of coverage to your existing network.
At its core is Amazon’s custom AZ3 silicon, with a new AI Accelerator built for on-device AI that sharpens conversational detection and filters out background noise.
Music, audiobooks, and podcasts sound great on the new Echo Dot, with crisp vocals and 50% more bass than its predecessor.
Echo Studio with Home Camera takes Amazon's best-sounding speaker and gives it a richer understanding of the room around it, making Alexa even more useful.
The camera enables a new Adaptive Volume feature that optimises playback as you move throughout the room.

What's new is context: with more awareness of its surroundings, Alexa can help in real time —explaining the rules on a board game box you hold up, recognizing a box of cereal to help you reorder it, or letting you check in on the room from the Alexa app while you're away.
Privacy is built into every Echo device from the ground up, and customers are in control of their experience.
There are clear visual indicators when Alexa is listening, and a dedicated privacy button turns the microphones off completely.

extraction.body: Apple on Tuesday unveiled its new 14-inch MacBook Pro, powered by its latest M6 chip. The new MacBook Pro has 24 hours of battery life and now supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity. The laptop starts at $1,999 and is available in space black and silver. Apple also announced its latest iMac , which is also powered by the M6 chip. The tech giant revealed the new devices just a day before its “Pro and Tell” event scheduled for Wednesday. On Monday, Apple announced its new iPad mini . The tech giant says the M6 chip features a 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core and a 12-core GPU that delivers more responsive performance, up to 30% faster graphics, and up to 25% faster AI workloads compared with the M5 chip. The M6 delivers up to 13 times the LLM prompt-processing speed of the M1 MacBook Pro and up to 1.3 times faster performance than the M5 model, Apple says. The M6 MacBook Pro starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, and has memory bandwidth of up to 170GB/s, up from the 153GB/s on the M5 chip. It includes HDMI, MagSafe 3, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, an SDXC card slot, and a headphone jack. Like previous models, the laptop features a 12-megapixel camera. The M6 MacBook Pro supports fast charging, reaching up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with a compatible high-wattage USB-C power adapter. As for the new M6-powered iMac, it features a faster CPU and GPU, with Neural Accelerators built into every core. Apple says the M6 delivers smooth multitasking and powerful performance for everyday apps, photo editing, and video production. The new iMac starts at $1,499 and comes in blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver. The company also notes that the new iMac delivers up to five times faster on-device AI performance than the M4 model. It features a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, an advanced camera and audio system, up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports, color-matched accessories, and macOS 27. Both the new MacBook Pro and iMac can be preordered starting October 28 and will be available starting November 6. Aisha is a consumer news reporter at TechCrunch. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, 6 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 7 and designed to be recycled.

The company also notes that the new iMac delivers up to five times faster on-device AI performance than the M4 model. It features a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, an advanced camera and audio system, up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports, color-matched accessories, and macOS 27. sources.title: Hands-on with Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro
passages: The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display weighs just 3 pounds, which is noticeably lighter than the current generation of non-touch MacBook Pros, which start at 3.4 pounds for the newly introduced M6 models.
Touch works almost exactly like you’d expect it to with Apple’s first-party apps.
Steve Jobs famously called touchscreen laptops “ergonomically terrible,” and for over a decade, Apple stridently refused to make one.
Today that all changes with the MacBook Pro — the company’s first laptop to embrace a touch interface.
That’s why it’s just a MacBook Pro variant and not an entirely new product line.
And while MacBook Pro hinges are pretty solid, yes, you can make it wobble pretty easily with some firm taps toward the top of the screen.
While it’s unlikely that Apple can fix all the “terrible” ergonomics of having to lift your arm up and touch a laptop screen, the company has put some effort into making macOS more touch-friendly.

Apple is trying to address this, at least slightly, by magnifying some controls when you poke at them — like the red, yellow, and green traffic light buttons in the top left corner of windows to close, minimize, and maximize an app.
On first impression, at least, the touchscreen doesn’t seem likely to revolutionize the MacBook.

extraction.body: Steve Jobs famously called touchscreen laptops “ergonomically terrible,” and for over a decade, Apple stridently refused to make one. Today that all changes with the MacBook Pro — the company’s first laptop to embrace a touch interface. While it’s unlikely that Apple can fix all the “terrible” ergonomics of having to lift your arm up and touch a laptop screen, the company has put some effort into making macOS more touch-friendly. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display weighs just 3 pounds, which is noticeably lighter than the current generation of non-touch MacBook Pros, which start at 3.4 pounds for the newly introduced M6 models. The difference is even bigger when you jump to the 16-inch model, which clocks in at 4 pounds, while the M5 Pro version without a touchscreen is 4.7. It still has heft, but it feels better balanced when picking it up from a corner with one hand. Putting it side by side with a current 16-inch MacBook Pro, you see that it’s slightly thinner and has a footprint a smidge smaller. It’s a seemingly minor feature, but one that definitely got the audience excited during the introduction, and marks the return of a bit of flair to the MacBook lineup, which, let’s be fair, has grown a bit utilitarian-looking over the years. Touch works almost exactly like you’d expect it to with Apple’s first-party apps. That said, anyone who has tried to “click” a tiny button in an app with their finger knows it’s a pretty fiddly experience at best and infuriating at worst. Apple is trying to address this, at least slightly, by magnifying some controls when you poke at them — like the red, yellow, and green traffic light buttons in the top left corner of windows to close, minimize, and maximize an app. And while MacBook Pro hinges are pretty solid, yes, you can make it wobble pretty easily with some firm taps toward the top of the screen. The OLED is punchy, bright, contrasty, and saturated. Without more time to do side-by-side comparisons, it’s hard to tell just how much of an improvement the OLED XDR display is. On first impression, at least, the touchscreen doesn’t seem likely to revolutionize the MacBook. That’s why it’s just a MacBook Pro variant and not an entirely new product line. Unsurprisingly, there is a price premium for the new MacBook Pro PROLED XDR. The touchscreen OLED model starts at $2,899, $400 more than the otherwise similarly-specced M5 Pro MacBook Pro.

extraction.body: It’s not as different from the previous model as you might have expected. LOS ANGELES—For about five minutes on an extremely crowded showroom floor, I got to take pictures of the new MacBook Pro and test out some of its new features. First impressions: It’s not as much of a departure from the previous design as I expected, but the outstanding OLED display steals the show regardless. The first thing I noticed was that it’s lighter. My daily driver is a 14-inch MacBook Pro (M1 Max), and it’s a bit weighty for a 14-incher. Picking up the new model, I could immediately tell it was lighter. It’s not like it’s in a different general weight class, but it’s a noticeable difference. The next thing I noticed was the Dynamic Island. Given the larger screen real estate of a laptop, it’s much less dominant on the screen than it is on an iPhone. I do worry about what will happen with fullscreen games, which I wasn’t able to test today. The notch MacBook Pro has an option to maximize apps or games to just below the notch, so it doesn’t cut into the image. I’m curious to test in the full review whether that remains the case with this little cutout. And lastly, the Apple logo on the back glows again! Some find this tacky, some find it essential. I just think it’s a little bit nostalgic. Of course, you might make the case that the most notable thing about this laptop is not its weight or the Dynamic Island. For years, people have debated whether Apple should introduce a touchscreen laptop. Steve Jobs was famously against it. A few years ago—there were reports that under Tim Cook and now John Ternus—Apple decided to move ahead with the idea. I played with it a bit, and it works just about exactly as you expect for a laptop touchscreen. A few of the things I did with the touchscreen during my brief time with the laptop: All of that is nice to have, I guess, but there’s not much you can do with it that you couldn’t already do with trackpad gestures, at least at the OS level; some creative apps, like finger painting on the screen, seemed to offer a bit more. When the credible reports emerged that the MacBook Pro would get a touchscreen, I imagined a convertible with Apple Pencil support—something you could use as a large iPad or drawing tablet, essentially. That’s not what this is; it only takes the usual laptop shape, and I was told it does not support the Apple Pencil. It’s just a MacBook Pro, in its normal form factor, but you can use your fingers on the screen to do things like drag files around, swipe between desktop spaces, or pinch-to-zoom on maps or images. But while it’s not about the touchscreen capability for me, I was impressed by the OLED screen itself—and I’m quite the display snob, if I’m being honest. The peak brightness, absolute blacks, well-balanced color, and dynamic range were genuinely remarkable. It’s an enormous upgrade over the MiniLED screen in the previous MacBook Pro. It took far too long for OLED to come to the MacBook Pro, but unsurprisingly, Apple spared no expense and cut no immediately obvious corners on quality. I was also happy to see that the cutout near the top of the screen that has replaced the camera notch is what Apple calls a Dynamic Island; it can resize to show live activities and other information on the fly. That’s one of my favorite features on the iPhone, as I’ve been impressed with Apple’s ability to turn something that should be an albatross into an appealing feature. Based on my time with the device and today’s announcement, the screen seems to be the main draw (though it’s nice that it noticeably weighs less, too), but the price is the real barrier. A 16-inch model with an M5 Max, 64 GB of RAM, and 2 TB of storage is currently priced at $5,799. Sure, that’s a high-end spec, but that’s some serious cash. Much of that is due to the storage and memory; upgrading from 64GB to 128GB adds a whopping $1,600 to that. Sure, most people don’t need anywhere near that much RAM—but some might for future-proofing for local AI workflows. I’m looking forward to spending more time with the new MacBook Pro, but for right now, it seems to follow in the lineup’s existing tradition: impressively high-end components like an outstanding OLED panel, but a very steep price to match. No surprises here! Though after well over a decade of speculation and back-and-forth, you’d be forgiven for being surprised that the touchscreen thing actually finally happened. After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.

extraction.body: Touchscreen on the MacBook for the first time. Apple today announced what Steve Jobs once dismissed as pointless: a touchscreen laptop. The new MacBook Pro comes in the same 14-inch and 16-inch screen size as before, but they feature brand new OLED displays and multitouch support (both for the first time ever in the MacBook line). An OLED panel, in short, produces deeper, truer blacks and more vibrant colors than conventional LCD or LED displays which previous Apple laptops have used. OLED panels are also lighter and thinner, thus allowing Apple to shed a bit of weight from the new MacBooks: the 14-inch model weighs just 3lbs and the larger model tips the scales at 4lbs. With multitouch support, users can interact with the MacBook screen very similar to the way they would an iPhone or iPad: you can pinch and zoom on photos, quickly swipe a window away, or more importantly, interact with Apple's popular line of creative apps like Final Cut Pro with your digits instead of a mouse arrow. I got brief hands-on time with the laptops, and the new displays are definitely impressive. They get up to 2000 nits of brightness, and the deeper blacks allow the screen to show contrast in ways previous MacBooks could not. The touch gesture felt second nature to anyone who has used an iPad, and Apple has redesigned some MacBook UI elements to make it easier for our fingers, like small buttons that automatically enlarge if it senses a finger. You still have the usual array of ports: a trio of Thunderbolt 5 USB-Cs; MagSafe; HDMI; a headphone jack and an SDXC memory card slot. The new MacBook Pros are powered by the M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, and they start at $2,899 for the 14-inch or $3,399 for the 16-inch. I'll be back with a full review hopefully in a couple of weeks. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

An OLED panel, in short, produces deeper, truer blacks and more vibrant colors than conventional LCD or LED displays which previous Apple laptops have used. OLED panels are also lighter and thinner, thus allowing Apple to shed a bit of weight from the new MacBooks: the 14-inch model weighs just 3lbs and the larger model tips the scales at 4lbs.

With multitouch support, users can interact with the MacBook screen very similar to the way they would an iPhone or iPad: you can pinch and zoom on photos, quickly swipe a window away, or more importantly, interact with Apple's popular line of creative apps like Final Cut Pro with your digits instead of a mouse arrow.

I got brief hands-on time with the laptops, and the new displays are definitely impressive. They get up to 2000 nits of brightness, and the deeper blacks allow the screen to show contrast in ways previous MacBooks could not.

The touch gesture felt second nature to anyone who has used an iPad, and Apple has redesigned some MacBook UI elements to make it easier for our fingers, like small buttons that automatically enlarge if it senses a finger. You still have the usual array of ports: a trio of Thunderbolt 5 USB-Cs; MagSafe; HDMI; a headphone jack and an SDXC memory card slot.
The new MacBook Pros are powered by the M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, and they start at $2,899 for the 14-inch or $3,399 for the 16-inch. I'll be back with a full review hopefully in a couple of weeks.

sources.title: Touchscreen MacBook Pro hands-on: OLED looks great on a Mac
passages: I’m looking forward to spending more time with the new MacBook Pro, but for right now, it seems to follow in the lineup’s existing tradition: impressively high-end components like an outstanding OLED panel, but a very steep price to match.
Though after well over a decade of speculation and back-and-forth, you’d be forgiven for being surprised that the touchscreen thing actually finally happened.
But while it’s not about the touchscreen capability for me, I was impressed by the OLED screen itself—and I’m quite the display snob, if I’m being honest.
The peak brightness, absolute blacks, well-balanced color, and dynamic range were genuinely remarkable.

When the credible reports emerged that the MacBook Pro would get a touchscreen, I imagined a convertible with Apple Pencil support—something you could use as a large iPad or drawing tablet, essentially.

extraction.body: It’s not as different from the previous model as you might have expected. LOS ANGELES—For about five minutes on an extremely crowded showroom floor, I got to take pictures of the new MacBook Pro and test out some of its new features. First impressions: It’s not as much of a departure from the previous design as I expected, but the outstanding OLED display steals the show regardless. The first thing I noticed was that it’s lighter. My daily driver is a 14-inch MacBook Pro (M1 Max), and it’s a bit weighty for a 14-incher. Picking up the new model, I could immediately tell it was lighter. It’s not like it’s in a different general weight class, but it’s a noticeable difference. The next thing I noticed was the Dynamic Island. Given the larger screen real estate of a laptop, it’s much less dominant on the screen than it is on an iPhone. I do worry about what will happen with fullscreen games, which I wasn’t able to test today. The notch MacBook Pro has an option to maximize apps or games to just below the notch, so it doesn’t cut into the image. I’m curious to test in the full review whether that remains the case with this little cutout. And lastly, the Apple logo on the back glows again! Some find this tacky, some find it essential. I just think it’s a little bit nostalgic. Of course, you might make the case that the most notable thing about this laptop is not its weight or the Dynamic Island. For years, people have debated whether Apple should introduce a touchscreen laptop. Steve Jobs was famously against it. A few years ago—there were reports that under Tim Cook and now John Ternus—Apple decided to move ahead with the idea. I played with it a bit, and it works just about exactly as you expect for a laptop touchscreen. A few of the things I did with the touchscreen during my brief time with the laptop: All of that is nice to have, I guess, but there’s not much you can do with it that you couldn’t already do with trackpad gestures, at least at the OS level; some creative apps, like finger painting on the screen, seemed to offer a bit more. When the credible reports emerged that the MacBook Pro would get a touchscreen, I imagined a convertible with Apple Pencil support—something you could use as a large iPad or drawing tablet, essentially. That’s not what this is; it only takes the usual laptop shape, and I was told it does not support the Apple Pencil. It’s just a MacBook Pro, in its normal form factor, but you can use your fingers on the screen to do things like drag files around, swipe between desktop spaces, or pinch-to-zoom on maps or images. But while it’s not about the touchscreen capability for me, I was impressed by the OLED screen itself—and I’m quite the display snob, if I’m being honest. The peak brightness, absolute blacks, well-balanced color, and dynamic range were genuinely remarkable. It’s an enormous upgrade over the MiniLED screen in the previous MacBook Pro. It took far too long for OLED to come to the MacBook Pro, but unsurprisingly, Apple spared no expense and cut no immediately obvious corners on quality. I was also happy to see that the cutout near the top of the screen that has replaced the camera notch is what Apple calls a Dynamic Island; it can resize to show live activities and other information on the fly. That’s one of my favorite features on the iPhone, as I’ve been impressed with Apple’s ability to turn something that should be an albatross into an appealing feature. Based on my time with the device and today’s announcement, the screen seems to be the main draw (though it’s nice that it noticeably weighs less, too), but the price is the real barrier. A 16-inch model with an M5 Max, 64 GB of RAM, and 2 TB of storage is currently priced at $5,799. Sure, that’s a high-end spec, but that’s some serious cash. Much of that is due to the storage and memory; upgrading from 64GB to 128GB adds a whopping $1,600 to that. Sure, most people don’t need anywhere near that much RAM—but some might for future-proofing for local AI workflows. I’m looking forward to spending more time with the new MacBook Pro, but for right now, it seems to follow in the lineup’s existing tradition: impressively high-end components like an outstanding OLED panel, but a very steep price to match. No surprises here! Though after well over a decade of speculation and back-and-forth, you’d be forgiven for being surprised that the touchscreen thing actually finally happened. extraction.body: Touchscreen on the MacBook for the first time. Apple today announced what Steve Jobs once dismissed as pointless: a touchscreen laptop. The new MacBook Pro comes in the same 14-inch and 16-inch screen size as before, but they feature brand new OLED displays and multitouch support (both for the first time ever in the MacBook line). An OLED panel, in short, produces deeper, truer blacks and more vibrant colors than conventional LCD or LED displays which previous Apple laptops have used. OLED panels are also lighter and thinner, thus allowing Apple to shed a bit of weight from the new MacBooks: the 14-inch model weighs just 3lbs and the larger model tips the scales at 4lbs. With multitouch support, users can interact with the MacBook screen very similar to the way they would an iPhone or iPad: you can pinch and zoom on photos, quickly swipe a window away, or more importantly, interact with Apple's popular line of creative apps like Final Cut Pro with your digits instead of a mouse arrow. Apple finally has touchscreen laptops. At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers. The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov. 6. The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399. The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory. These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. They also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016. The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2-and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks. They also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016.

extraction.body: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with its Touch Bar on a MacBook Pro , which it later went on to remove . The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes. The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage. The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display. In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound. The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors. Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant. The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399. Consumers can place a preorder for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6. Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past.
The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes.
The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.
The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

extraction.body: Apple has (finally) just announced the product that all tech enthusiasts have been talking about since last year: a MacBook with a touchscreen. The company quietly unveiled the device at its Pro And Tell event held in Los Angeles on October 28. What was earlier expected to be a livestream event by the media turned into a rather quick announcement from the Cupertino-based tech giant.Johny Srouji, Apple rsquo;s chief hardware officer, said in a press release, The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a monumental step forward for the Mac. PROLED XDR is the world rsquo;s best laptop display. It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of.Apple launches Touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED screenThe new MacBook Pro with a PROLED rsquo; screen is already visible on Apple rsquo;s official website. The price of the device starts from Rs 3,49,900 for the 14-inch variant, whereas the 16-inch model starts from Rs 4,09,900. Apple has also included a detail that will delight all those who loved the earlier MacBooks. The 2017 MacBook Air, powered by Intel, was the last model that carried the illuminating logo which was loved by many. Now that it has made a comeback after nearly a decade, it will make some long-term Apple fans really happy.You can pre-order the touchscreen MacBook starting today, and it will be available from November 9 this year.Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch: Specs and top featuresThe 14-inch MacBook Pro is powered by Apples M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, with multiple configurations available depending on the performance you need. The M5 Pro comes with either a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU or an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU. The M5 Max, meanwhile, features an 18-core CPU and is available with a 32-core or 40-core GPU. All configurations include a 16-core Neural Engine, Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. Memory bandwidth reaches 307GB/s on the M5 Pro and up to 614GB/s on the M5 Max.The laptop is available with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of SSD storage. The M5 Pro variants offer 24GB, 48GB or 64GB of memory, while the M5 Max models come with 36GB, 48GB, 64GB or 128GB options. Storage starts at 1TB on M5 Pro models and 2TB on M5 Max models.The 14-inch MacBook Pro features a 14.2-inch PROLED XDR display with a 3024 times; 1986 resolution and a pixel density of 254ppi. The tandem OLED panel supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates of up to 120Hz, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and up to 2,000 nits peak brightness for HDR content. It also supports one billion colours, P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts, True Tone and Multi-Touch gestures. The display comes with an anti-reflective and fingerprint-resistant coating, with a nano-texture glass option available.For battery life, the M5 Pro model is rated to deliver up to 22 hours of video streaming and 14 hours of wireless web browsing. Both use a 72.6Wh battery and support fast charging with a 96W or higher USB PD power source.Connectivity options include three Thunderbolt 5 USB-C ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, a MagSafe 3 charging port and a 3.5mm headphone jack. The MacBook Pro also supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apples N1 wireless networking chip. The M5 Pro model supports up to three external displays, while the M5 Max variant can connect up to four.Touchscreen MacBook Pro 16-inch: Specs and top featuresThe 16-inch MacBook Pro is powered by Apples M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. The M5 Pro features an 18-core CPU and a 20-core GPU, while the M5 Max is available with an 18-core CPU and either a 32-core or 40-core GPU. All configurations include a 16-core Neural Engine, Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. Memory bandwidth reaches 307GB/s on the M5 Pro and up to 614GB/s on the M5 Max.The laptop is available with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of SSD storage. The M5 Pro variant offers 24GB, 48GB or 64GB of memory, while the M5 Max models come with 36GB, 48GB, 64GB or 128GB options. Storage starts at 1TB on M5 Pro models and 2TB on M5 Max models.The 16-inch MacBook Pro features a 16.3-inch PROLED XDR display with a 3472 times; 2266 resolution and a pixel density of 254ppi. The tandem OLED panel supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates of up to 120Hz, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and up to 2,000 nits peak brightness for HDR content. It also supports one billion colours, P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts, True Tone and Multi-Touch gestures. The display comes with an anti-reflective and fingerprint-resistant coating, with a nano-texture glass option available.For battery life, the M5 Pro model is rated to deliver up to 24 hours of video streaming and 17 hours of wireless web browsing. The M5 Max variant is rated for up to 22 hours of video streaming and 16 hours of wireless web browsing. The 14-inch model is lighter and more compact, and it also offers an additional M5 Pro configuration with a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU. Both models share the same core display technology, connectivity options and top-end M5 Max configurations.

sources.title: Apple launches its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, from $2,899 - The Next Web
passages: Apple unveiled a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, an OLED display and a Dynamic Island, after two decades of rejecting touch Macs.
The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and weighs 3 pounds; the 16-inch starts at $3,399.
The model sits above the M6 MacBook Pro launched on Tuesday, which keeps a regular screen and costs from $1,999.
Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November.
The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.
Its macOS interface has been reworked for touch, so users can tap, scroll and pinch to zoom, and many existing apps work with touch straight away.

It is also the first Mac with an OLED screen and a Dynamic Island, the strip at the top of iPhone displays that shows alerts and controls. The laptop comes in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips. The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and the 16-inch at $3,399, Apple said . Chief hardware officer Johny Srouji called it a “ monumental step forward for the Mac. ” New chief executive John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook last month, presented it on stage. The launch reverses a long-held view at Apple. Steve Jobs once called touchscreen laptops “ ergonomically terrible, ” and Cook compared merging a laptop and a tablet to combining a fridge and a toaster. In 2016, design chief Jony Ive said a touchscreen Mac would not be useful . Cook and Ternus began backing a touchscreen MacBook Pro about four years ago, Bloomberg reported, hoping to revive Mac sales and charge more for premium features. coreStoryFacts.text: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.
At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

A lover of all things gaming and tech, his previous work has shown up in Tom's Guide, Laptop Mag, Kotaku, PCMag and Complex, among others.

The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well).
