Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks.

Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more.
Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound.
There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed.
After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899.
The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September .
Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past.
The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes.
The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.
The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

The price of the device starts from Rs 3,49,900 for the 14-inch variant, whereas the 16-inch model starts from Rs 4,09,900.
The MacBook Pro also supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apples N1 wireless networking chip.
Apple has also included a detail that will delight all those who loved the earlier MacBooks.
Apple unveiled a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, an OLED display and a Dynamic Island, after two decades of rejecting touch Macs.
The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and weighs 3 pounds; the 16-inch starts at $3,399.
The model sits above the M6 MacBook Pro launched on Tuesday, which keeps a regular screen and costs from $1,999.
Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November.
The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.
Its macOS interface has been reworked for touch, so users can tap, scroll and pinch to zoom, and many existing apps work with touch straight away.

coreFacts.text: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov.
The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399.
The systems use Apple's existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and go up to 16TB of storage and 128GB of memory.
These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch.
These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications.
At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers.
Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before.
The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo).
In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it.
The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor.

Apple finally has touchscreen laptops. At an event in Los Angeles, the company detailed its new MacBook Pros featuring OLED XDR displays that you can control with your fingers. The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros are available for pre-order now and will ship on Nov. 6. The 14-incher will start at $2,899, while the 16-incher will start at $3,399. These systems also feature the first redesigns for the MacBook Pro since 2021, when the M1 Pro and M1 Max launched in what has become a familiar design with a notch. These new models include the Dynamic Island around the webcam, similar to the iPhone, which can be used for real-time notifications. They also have light-up Apple logos, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro since 2016. The PROLED XDR display comes in 14.2-and 16.3-inch sizes, with ProMotion allowing for refresh rates between 10 Hz and 120 Hz. Apple claims 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for intensely deep blacks. The 14-inch MacBook Pro is 3 pounds, about half a pound less than the existing version, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro is 4 pounds, or 0.7 pounds lighter than it was before. Apple's bezels are also less noticeable than before. The hinge seems to be a point of pride (that's the second time this month, after the iPhone Duo). In this case, it's that the screen is less prone to wobble when you touch it. The new laptops are only slightly thinner than their predecessor. Apple claims that the 16-inch model is "nearly a millimeter thinner" and the 14-incher is "half a millimeter thinner." Apple attributes those shavings to OLED's display stack. Apple's own apps are already set to work with touch out of the box, and the company says many other apps will already work right away, including Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, and more. Apple already had the best speakers in a laptop, and now it's promising improvements: 50% deeper bass and new tweeters for clearer sound. There's even dedicated audio tuning for people who want to use the speakers with their laptop lid closed. The significant change to the Mac is another in a flurry of launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also recently introduced the iPhone 18 Pro; the foldable iPhone Duo; Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4; HomeView; and a new iPad Mini, also with an OLED panel. The devices follow a long resistance to touchscreen laptops from Apple. Former CEO Steve Jobs, at an event introducing Mac OS X Lion in 2010, called laptops with touchscreens "ergonomically terrible" , claiming that "after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off." (HomeView, Apple's smart home manager, has a vertical touchscreen and no one has made a peep about that. The iPad, too, has been vertical on Apple's keyboards, though some of those include touchpads as well). The Mac resisted a touchscreen throughout former CEO Tim Cook's tenure, as well, though these new laptops definitely were developed under his leadership. In the last decade, touchscreens have become a common feature on laptops running Windows, and Microsoft's latest operating system, Windows 11 , was designed to be slightly more touch-friendly than its predecessors. sources.title: Apple launches its new touchscreen MacBook Pro
passages: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899.
The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September .
Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past.
The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes.
The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage.
The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.

extraction.body: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with its Touch Bar on a MacBook Pro , which it later went on to remove . The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes. The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage. The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display. In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound. The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors. Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant. The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399. Consumers can place a preorder for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6. The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September . Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past. Jobs famously called the idea “ergonomically terrible” at one point. However, rumors of the company working on such a variant started circulating nearly three years before today’s introduction . The launch follows yesterday’s unveiling of a new standard MacBook Pro with the M6 chip in 14-inch size starting from $1,999 . extraction.body: Apple has (finally) just announced the product that all tech enthusiasts have been talking about since last year: a MacBook with a touchscreen. The company quietly unveiled the device at its Pro And Tell event held in Los Angeles on October 28. What was earlier expected to be a livestream event by the media turned into a rather quick announcement from the Cupertino-based tech giant.Johny Srouji, Apple rsquo;s chief hardware officer, said in a press release, The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a monumental step forward for the Mac. PROLED XDR is the world rsquo;s best laptop display. It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of.Apple launches Touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED screenThe new MacBook Pro with a PROLED rsquo; screen is already visible on Apple rsquo;s official website. The price of the device starts from Rs 3,49,900 for the 14-inch variant, whereas the 16-inch model starts from Rs 4,09,900. Apple has also included a detail that will delight all those who loved the earlier MacBooks. The 2017 MacBook Air, powered by Intel, was the last model that carried the illuminating logo which was loved by many. Now that it has made a comeback after nearly a decade, it will make some long-term Apple fans really happy.You can pre-order the touchscreen MacBook starting today, and it will be available from November 9 this year.Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch: Specs and top featuresThe 14-inch MacBook Pro is powered by Apples M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, with multiple configurations available depending on the performance you need. The M5 Pro comes with either a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU or an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU. The M5 Max, meanwhile, features an 18-core CPU and is available with a 32-core or 40-core GPU. All configurations include a 16-core Neural Engine, Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. Memory bandwidth reaches 307GB/s on the M5 Pro and up to 614GB/s on the M5 Max.The laptop is available with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of SSD storage. The M5 Pro variants offer 24GB, 48GB or 64GB of memory, while the M5 Max models come with 36GB, 48GB, 64GB or 128GB options. Storage starts at 1TB on M5 Pro models and 2TB on M5 Max models.The 14-inch MacBook Pro features a 14.2-inch PROLED XDR display with a 3024 times; 1986 resolution and a pixel density of 254ppi. The tandem OLED panel supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates of up to 120Hz, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and up to 2,000 nits peak brightness for HDR content. It also supports one billion colours, P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts, True Tone and Multi-Touch gestures. The display comes with an anti-reflective and fingerprint-resistant coating, with a nano-texture glass option available.For battery life, the M5 Pro model is rated to deliver up to 22 hours of video streaming and 14 hours of wireless web browsing. Both use a 72.6Wh battery and support fast charging with a 96W or higher USB PD power source.Connectivity options include three Thunderbolt 5 USB-C ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, a MagSafe 3 charging port and a 3.5mm headphone jack. The MacBook Pro also supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apples N1 wireless networking chip. The M5 Pro model supports up to three external displays, while the M5 Max variant can connect up to four.Touchscreen MacBook Pro 16-inch: Specs and top featuresThe 16-inch MacBook Pro is powered by Apples M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. The M5 Pro features an 18-core CPU and a 20-core GPU, while the M5 Max is available with an 18-core CPU and either a 32-core or 40-core GPU. All configurations include a 16-core Neural Engine, Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. Memory bandwidth reaches 307GB/s on the M5 Pro and up to 614GB/s on the M5 Max.The laptop is available with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of SSD storage. The M5 Pro variant offers 24GB, 48GB or 64GB of memory, while the M5 Max models come with 36GB, 48GB, 64GB or 128GB options. Storage starts at 1TB on M5 Pro models and 2TB on M5 Max models.The 16-inch MacBook Pro features a 16.3-inch PROLED XDR display with a 3472 times; 2266 resolution and a pixel density of 254ppi. The tandem OLED panel supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates of up to 120Hz, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio and up to 2,000 nits peak brightness for HDR content. It also supports one billion colours, P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts, True Tone and Multi-Touch gestures. The display comes with an anti-reflective and fingerprint-resistant coating, with a nano-texture glass option available.For battery life, the M5 Pro model is rated to deliver up to 24 hours of video streaming and 17 hours of wireless web browsing. The M5 Max variant is rated for up to 22 hours of video streaming and 16 hours of wireless web browsing. The 14-inch model is lighter and more compact, and it also offers an additional M5 Pro configuration with a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU. Both models share the same core display technology, connectivity options and top-end M5 Max configurations.

passages: Apple unveiled a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, an OLED display and a Dynamic Island, after two decades of rejecting touch Macs.
The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and weighs 3 pounds; the 16-inch starts at $3,399.
The model sits above the M6 MacBook Pro launched on Tuesday, which keeps a regular screen and costs from $1,999.
Pre-orders are open now, with deliveries from 6 November.
The launch caps a busy week for Apple, which also released a new OLED iPad mini on Monday, as part of a wider overhaul of its Mac line.
Its macOS interface has been reworked for touch, so users can tap, scroll and pinch to zoom, and many existing apps work with touch straight away.

extraction.body: The Trump administration is giving Constellation Energy $5 billion in loans to expand nuclear generating capacity at eight power plants by 1.1 gigawatts. Most or all of the additional power from seven of those facilities has already been bought by Google, Meta, or Amazon. Constellation said it plans to use the financing to “uprate” 11 existing reactors, an industry term for expanding capacity at a reactor, often by using more highly enriched uranium and by upgrading equipment to handle the increased power levels. The energy company said it had already committed to spending more than $7 billion to add 1,080 megawatts of nuclear capacity to deliver power to Google, Amazon, and Meta. The loan commitment, which has yet to be finalized, “could lower financing costs” for the projects, Constellation said in a press release . The eight power plants include six in Illinois (Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, La Salle, and Quad Cities), one in Maryland (Calvert Cliffs), and one in Pennsylvania (Limerick). Google is already the confirmed buyer of additional power from the Pennsylvania plant and four Illinois power plants, while Amazon is buying electricity from the Maryland plant and Meta is effectively buying the entire Clinton power plant in Illinois. On Tuesday, the Department of Energy touted the loan as supporting “affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses,” though there is no evidence that the new nuclear capacity will lower prices for residential ratepayers. Constellation’s announcement does not say whether the projects will maintain or lower electricity rates, and the company would not confirm the government’s claim to TechCrunch. Hyperscalers, including Google, Amazon, and Meta, have been scouring the grid for additional capacity to support their AI data centers. Tech companies are paying handsomely for energy, committing tens of billions of dollars over the coming years. Given that power has become a competitive advantage, that estimate is probably on the low end. By lowering the cost of capital for the upgrades, the Department of Energy’s loans could boost Constellation’s bottom line, that of the hyperscalers — or both. He has written for a wide range of publications, including Wired magazine, the Chicago Tribune, Ars Technica, The Wire China, and NOVA Next, where he was founding editor. De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College. extraction.body: The Trump administration is giving Constellation Energy $5 billion in loans to expand nuclear generating capacity at eight power plants by 1.1 gigawatts. Most or all of the additional power from seven of those facilities has already been bought by Google, Meta, or Amazon. Constellation said it plans to use the financing to “uprate” 11 existing reactors, an industry term for expanding capacity at a reactor, often by using more highly enriched uranium and by upgrading equipment to handle the increased power levels. The energy company said it had already committed to spending more than $7 billion to add 1,080 megawatts of nuclear capacity to deliver power to Google, Amazon, and Meta. The loan commitment, which has yet to be finalized, “could lower financing costs” for the projects, Constellation said in a press release . The eight power plants include six in Illinois (Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, La Salle, and Quad Cities), one in Maryland (Calvert Cliffs), and one in Pennsylvania (Limerick). Google is already the confirmed buyer of additional power from the Pennsylvania plant and four Illinois power plants, while Amazon is buying electricity from the Maryland plant and Meta is effectively buying the entire Clinton power plant in Illinois. On Tuesday, the Department of Energy touted the loan as supporting “affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses,” though there is no evidence that the new nuclear capacity will lower prices for residential ratepayers. Constellation’s announcement does not say whether the projects will maintain or lower electricity rates, and the company would not confirm the government’s claim to TechCrunch. Hyperscalers, including Google, Amazon, and Meta, have been scouring the grid for additional capacity to support their AI data centers. Tech companies are paying handsomely for energy, committing tens of billions of dollars over the coming years. Given that power has become a competitive advantage, that estimate is probably on the low end. By lowering the cost of capital for the upgrades, the Department of Energy’s loans could boost Constellation’s bottom line, that of the hyperscalers — or both. Tim De Chant is a senior climate reporter at TechCrunch. He has written for a wide range of publications, including Wired magazine, the Chicago Tribune, Ars Technica, The Wire China, and NOVA Next, where he was founding editor. De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College. The eight power plants include six in Illinois (Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, La Salle, and Quad Cities), one in Maryland (Calvert Cliffs), and one in Pennsylvania (Limerick).

Google is already the confirmed buyer of additional power from the Pennsylvania plant and four Illinois power plants, while Amazon is buying electricity from the Maryland plant and Meta is effectively buying the entire Clinton power plant in Illinois.

On Tuesday, the Department of Energy touted the loan as supporting “affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses,” though there is no evidence that the new nuclear capacity will lower prices for residential ratepayers. Constellation’s announcement does not say whether the projects will maintain or lower electricity rates, and the company would not confirm the government’s claim to TechCrunch.

Hyperscalers, including Google, Amazon, and Meta, have been scouring the grid for additional capacity to support their AI data centers. Tech companies are paying handsomely for energy, committing tens of billions of dollars over the coming years. Given that power has become a competitive advantage, that estimate is probably on the low end.
By lowering the cost of capital for the upgrades, the Department of Energy’s loans could boost Constellation’s bottom line, that of the hyperscalers — or both.

De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College.

sources.body: Apple has announced refreshes for the iMac and the entry-level, 14-inch MacBook Pro . Both machines are getting the M6 chip, which was introduced in the Mac mini several weeks ago. In this case, that means up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to double the Neural Engine performance. Apple skipped the M5 and went straight to the M6 here. It caps out at 32GB of RAM but can go to 4TB of storage.

extraction.body: Additionally, the N1 chip brings Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Apple has announced refreshes for the iMac and the entry-level, 14-inch MacBook Pro . Both machines are getting the M6 chip, which was introduced in the Mac mini several weeks ago. The M6 is split into two variants for the iMac. Picking the “M6 chip with two Thunderbolt ports” option gets you a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, whereas picking “M6 chip with four Thunderbolt ports” gets you 12 cores for each, instead. The two-port variant maxes out at 24 GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, whereas the four-port one maxes out at 32GB of RAM and 2TB of storage. There’s only one M6 chip option for the MacBook Pro—the one with the 12-core GPU and CPU. It caps out at 32GB of RAM but can go to 4TB of storage. It’s a more substantial refresh for the iMac, as its previous update introduced the M4. Apple skipped the M5 and went straight to the M6 here. In terms of performance gains moving from the M4 to the M6, Apple said with the Mac mini that users can expect up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, up to double graphics performance, and nearly five times faster on-device AI. All that largely matches what we saw when we tested the M6 Mac mini last month, and users of the new iMac should expect similar numbers. The M6 iMac should see up to double SSD read/write performance compared to the M4 model, too. The previous entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro had the M5, so that one is just stepping up a single generation. In this case, that means up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to double the Neural Engine performance. In addition to the M6 chip, both computers now have the N1 chip for wireless connectivity (that means Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6). The iMac is now configurable with up to 2.5Gb Ethernet, while the MacBook Pro still lacks an Ethernet port. There are no outward design changes to either device; they both look exactly the same as their immediate predecessors. The iMac starts at $1,499 for the two-port version, or $1,699 for the four-port version. The M6 MacBook Pro starts at $1,999. Preorders start October 28, and they ship November 6. sources.title: Apple's M6 chip brings serious on-device AI power to the entry-level MacBook Pro and the colorful iMac - XDA
passages: Ahead of its upcoming "Pro and Tell" event, Apple has revealed its refreshed 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac , powered by its M6 chip.
This means the new MacBook Pro features three Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, a MagSafe 3 charging port, a full HDMI port, and an SD card slot.
While this isn't exactly surprising, given Apple's MacBook Pro design has been around for several years now, it would have been nice to see it evolve in some way.
Apple also refreshed its all-in-one iMac with the M6 chip .
This update comes two years after the colorful computer got the M4 chip (the iMac skipped the M5 series entirely).
The base M6 configuration in the iMac features a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, a step up from the 8-core M4 CPU in the last-generation iMac.

Apple says that the M6 features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, emphasizing that it's a powerful platform for local LLMs and that the chip is designed to take full advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.
The MacBook M6 also features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, alongside returning features like the 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and Liquid Retina XDR display with optional nano-texture.
The entry-level iMac starts at $1,500 and will be available to pre-order on October 28th, with shipping starting on November 6th.
Apple also recently revealed its A20-powered iPad mini .
At its upcoming event, the tech giant is expected to show off its long-rumored touchscreen MacBook for the first time.

extraction.body: Ahead of its upcoming "Pro and Tell" event, Apple has revealed its refreshed 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac , powered by its M6 chip. The tech giant says the M6 features a 12-core CPU, paired with a 12-core GPU that delivers 30 percent faster graphics and 25 percent faster AI workload performance compared to last year's M5 chip. Interestingly, the company also compares the M6 to the M1 in its press release, highlighting that the newer, more powerful chip offers 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance. Apple says that the M6 features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, emphasizing that it's a powerful platform for local LLMs and that the chip is designed to take full advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence. The MacBook M6 also features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, alongside returning features like the 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and Liquid Retina XDR display with optional nano-texture. Beyond the bump up to the M6 chip, the entry-level 14-inch MacBook features the same overall design and port layout as last year's M5 upgrade and, in fact, the year prior's M4 refresh. This means the new MacBook Pro features three Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, a MagSafe 3 charging port, a full HDMI port, and an SD card slot. While this isn't exactly surprising, given Apple's MacBook Pro design has been around for several years now, it would have been nice to see it evolve in some way. Pricing for the 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro starts at $2,000 for the 16GB version, which matches last year's pricing. Pre-orders start on October 28th, with shipping beginning on November 6th. Apple also refreshed its all-in-one iMac with the M6 chip . This update comes two years after the colorful computer got the M4 chip (the iMac skipped the M5 series entirely). The base M6 configuration in the iMac features a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, a step up from the 8-core M4 CPU in the last-generation iMac. There's also a more expensive 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU configuration Beyond the chip upgrade, there isn't much else new. The refreshed iMac features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 like the new 14-inch MacBook Pro. It also has the same Thunderbolt ports as the M4 iMac — two on the 10-core and four on the 12-core. The colors are all the same too: Blue, Purple, Pink, Orange, Yellow, Green, and Silver. At the very least, it would have been great to see an iMac color refresh and a port selection that made a bit more sense. The entry-level iMac starts at $1,500 and will be available to pre-order on October 28th, with shipping starting on November 6th. The M6 MacBook Pro and iMac follow the M6 Mac Mini that Apple revealed earlier this year, which the company somewhat confusingly showed off alongside the M5 Max and M5 Ultra Mac Studio. The M6 is Apple's first 2nm chip and bumps up to a 12-core CPU from the M5's 10 cores. Apple also recently revealed its A20-powered iPad mini . At its upcoming event, the tech giant is expected to show off its long-rumored touchscreen MacBook for the first time. The redesigned tablet also features a thinner and lighter design. I love my MacBook Pro M5 and hope it lasts me as long as my M1 did. What confuses me is why so much emphasis is put on the device's bigger, better performance, but most people are running most things online now, so the performance is surely about the weakest link... Usually the speed of the internet and connection at the time you are using it. Nobody really focuses on that. I'm sure my Antigravity work sessions would be improved greatly by a much better and consistent internet connection than a slightly faster processor in my Mac. Just food for thought.

The MacBook M6 also features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, alongside returning features like the 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and Liquid Retina XDR display with optional nano-texture.

Beyond the bump up to the M6 chip, the entry-level 14-inch MacBook features the same overall design and port layout as last year's M5 upgrade and, in fact, the year prior's M4 refresh. This means the new MacBook Pro features three Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, a MagSafe 3 charging port, a full HDMI port, and an SD card slot. While this isn't exactly surprising, given Apple's MacBook Pro design has been around for several years now, it would have been nice to see it evolve in some way.
Pricing for the 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro starts at $2,000 for the 16GB version, which matches last year's pricing. Pre-orders start on October 28th, with shipping beginning on November 6th.

Apple also refreshed its all-in-one iMac with the M6 chip . This update comes two years after the colorful computer got the M4 chip (the iMac skipped the M5 series entirely). The base M6 configuration in the iMac features a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, a step up from the 8-core M4 CPU in the last-generation iMac. There's also a more expensive 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU configuration

Beyond the chip upgrade, there isn't much else new. The refreshed iMac features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 like the new 14-inch MacBook Pro. It also has the same Thunderbolt ports as the M4 iMac — two on the 10-core and four on the 12-core. The colors are all the same too: Blue, Purple, Pink, Orange, Yellow, Green, and Silver. At the very least, it would have been great to see an iMac color refresh and a port selection that made a bit more sense.
The entry-level iMac starts at $1,500 and will be available to pre-order on October 28th, with shipping starting on November 6th.

The M6 MacBook Pro and iMac follow the M6 Mac Mini that Apple revealed earlier this year, which the company somewhat confusingly showed off alongside the M5 Max and M5 Ultra Mac Studio. The M6 is Apple's first 2nm chip and bumps up to a 12-core CPU from the M5's 10 cores.
Apple also recently revealed its A20-powered iPad mini . At its upcoming event, the tech giant is expected to show off its long-rumored touchscreen MacBook for the first time.
The redesigned tablet also features a thinner and lighter design.

I love my MacBook Pro M5 and hope it lasts me as long as my M1 did. What confuses me is why so much emphasis is put on the device's bigger, better performance, but most people are running most things online now, so the performance is surely about the weakest link... Usually the speed of the internet and connection at the time you are using it. Nobody really focuses on that. I'm sure my Antigravity work sessions would be improved greatly by a much better and consistent internet connection than a slightly faster processor in my Mac. Just food for thought.

extraction.body: On the heels of yesterday’s new iPad Mini , Apple has turned its attention to its Mac lineup. Unlike the iPad Mini that received an OLED display and a water-resistant design, today’s Mac updates are mere spec bumps. After debuting its M6 processor with the Mac Mini in August, Apple is bringing the new chip to both its entry-level MacBook Pro and iMac . The M6 chip in the ‌MacBook Pro‌ features a 12-core CPU (two super cores, four performance cores and six efficiency cores) and a 12-core GPU. The previous M5 model had a 10-core CPU (four super cores and six efficiency cores) and a 10-core GPU. In addition, the Neural Engine in the M6 doubles the number of cores, with a dual 16-core NE replacing the single 16-core NE from before. Memory bandwidth also increases from 153GB per second to 170GB per second, but this bump applies only when you choose to outfit the MacBook Pro with 24GB or 32GB of memory, not the default 16GB. Networking improves with support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and the new laptop can support dual external 4K displays at up to 165Hz, up from 144Hz. In this era of constantly rising costs , seeing a price remain constant feels like a win. The M6 MacBook Pro starts at the same $1,999 price as the previous model. It’s been nearly two years since the last iMac update, which means Apple’s all-in-one makes the jump from the M4 to the M6 processor. The design (built around a 24-inch, 4.5K Retina display) and color options (blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange and silver) stay the same, as does the $1,499 starting price. But now for that $1,499, the M6 iMac has a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU along with the dual 16-core Neural Engine. That’s up from the M4 chip, which started with eight CPU cores, eight GPU cores and a single 16-core NE. The step-up model costs $1,699 and gets you an M6 chip with a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, along with four Thunderbolt 4 ports instead of just a pair. This higher-end model also comes with 2.5Gbps Ethernet, which is available as an add-on with the baseline model. The previous M4 iMac offered only gigabit Ethernet. Preorders open Wednesday, Oct. 28, for the new M6 MacBook Pro and M6 iMac, with shipping expected to start on Friday, Nov. 6. Apple’s Pro and Tell week isn’t over. It will culminate with tomorrow’s special event in Los Angeles, where Apple is expected to reveal the long-awaited touchscreen MacBook Pro . © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.

The tech giant says the M6 features a 12-core CPU, paired with a 12-core GPU that delivers 30 percent faster graphics and 25 percent faster AI workload performance compared to last year's M5 chip. Interestingly, the company also compares the M6 to the M1 in its press release, highlighting that the newer, more powerful chip offers 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance. Apple says that the M6 features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, emphasizing that it's a powerful platform for local LLMs and that the chip is designed to take full advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence. The MacBook M6 also features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, alongside returning features like the 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and Liquid Retina XDR display with optional nano-texture. Beyond the bump up to the M6 chip, the entry-level 14-inch MacBook features the same overall design and port layout as last year's M5 upgrade and, in fact, the year prior's M4 refresh. This means the new MacBook Pro features three Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, a MagSafe 3 charging port, a full HDMI port, and an SD card slot. While this isn't exactly surprising, given Apple's MacBook Pro design has been around for several years now, it would have been nice to see it evolve in some way. Pricing for the 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro starts at $2,000 for the 16GB version, which matches last year's pricing. Pre-orders start on October 28th, with shipping beginning on November 6th. Apple also refreshed its all-in-one iMac with the M6 chip . This update comes two years after the colorful computer got the M4 chip (the iMac skipped the M5 series entirely). The base M6 configuration in the iMac features a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, a step up from the 8-core M4 CPU in the last-generation iMac. There's also a more expensive 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU configuration Beyond the chip upgrade, there isn't much else new. The refreshed iMac features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 like the new 14-inch MacBook Pro. It also has the same Thunderbolt ports as the M4 iMac — two on the 10-core and four on the 12-core. The colors are all the same too: Blue, Purple, Pink, Orange, Yellow, Green, and Silver. At the very least, it would have been great to see an iMac color refresh and a port selection that made a bit more sense. The entry-level iMac starts at $1,500 and will be available to pre-order on October 28th, with shipping starting on November 6th. The M6 MacBook Pro and iMac follow the M6 Mac Mini that Apple revealed earlier this year, which the company somewhat confusingly showed off alongside the M5 Max and M5 Ultra Mac Studio. The M6 is Apple's first 2nm chip and bumps up to a 12-core CPU from the M5's 10 cores. Apple also recently revealed its A20-powered iPad mini . At its upcoming event, the tech giant is expected to show off its long-rumored touchscreen MacBook for the first time. The redesigned tablet also features a thinner and lighter design. I love my MacBook Pro M5 and hope it lasts me as long as my M1 did. What confuses me is why so much emphasis is put on the device's bigger, better performance, but most people are running most things online now, so the performance is surely about the weakest link... Usually the speed of the internet and connection at the time you are using it. Nobody really focuses on that. I'm sure my Antigravity work sessions would be improved greatly by a much better and consistent internet connection than a slightly faster processor in my Mac. Just food for thought.

extraction.body: On the heels of yesterday’s new iPad Mini , Apple has turned its attention to its Mac lineup. Unlike the iPad Mini that received an OLED display and a water-resistant design, today’s Mac updates are mere spec bumps. After debuting its M6 processor with the Mac Mini in August, Apple is bringing the new chip to both its entry-level MacBook Pro and iMac . The M6 chip in the ‌MacBook Pro‌ features a 12-core CPU (two super cores, four performance cores and six efficiency cores) and a 12-core GPU. The previous M5 model had a 10-core CPU (four super cores and six efficiency cores) and a 10-core GPU. In addition, the Neural Engine in the M6 doubles the number of cores, with a dual 16-core NE replacing the single 16-core NE from before. Memory bandwidth also increases from 153GB per second to 170GB per second, but this bump applies only when you choose to outfit the MacBook Pro with 24GB or 32GB of memory, not the default 16GB. Networking improves with support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and the new laptop can support dual external 4K displays at up to 165Hz, up from 144Hz. In this era of constantly rising costs , seeing a price remain constant feels like a win. The M6 MacBook Pro starts at the same $1,999 price as the previous model. It’s been nearly two years since the last iMac update, which means Apple’s all-in-one makes the jump from the M4 to the M6 processor. The design (built around a 24-inch, 4.5K Retina display) and color options (blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange and silver) stay the same, as does the $1,499 starting price. But now for that $1,499, the M6 iMac has a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU along with the dual 16-core Neural Engine. extraction.body: This week, Apple released a series of new products in rapid succession, launching the 24-inch iMac and 14-inch entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip ahead of the touchscreen MacBook Pro's debut. Two new models will be available for pre-order at 1:10 AM on October 29, with official shipping beginning on November 6. The new iMac starts at RMB 12,499, and the MacBook Pro starts at RMB 15,999. Apple stated that the M6 chip enables the new iMac to deliver five times the performance on AI tasks compared to the previous generation, while the entry-level MacBook Pro offers a 30% improvement in graphics processing over its predecessor. This release is the second wave of Apple’s product launch campaign this week. On Monday, the company updated the iPad mini with an upgraded display and water-resistant features. Wall Street Journal noted that Apple will conclude its product releases this week on Wednesday with its first-ever touchscreen MacBook Pro. The new iMac and MacBook Pro closely resemble their predecessors in design, with main changes focused on internal hardware. Both models feature the M6 chip—first introduced in September alongside the Mac mini. In this update, the iMac has jumped from the M4 chip to the M6 chip, while the MacBook Pro only received the M5 chip last year, resulting in a relatively shorter iteration cycle. In terms of connectivity, both new devices support Bluetooth 6 and Wi-Fi 7, and the new MacBook Pro also features faster charging. Apple continues to sell the high-end MacBook Pro models equipped with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, both of which feature higher specifications for the main processor and graphics cores compared to the newly released entry-level M6 model. Apple will release its first MacBook Pro with a touchscreen this Wednesday, ending the company’s two-decade-long resistance to touchscreens on laptops. The new touch-screen MacBook Pro will feature a lighter and thinner design, narrower screen bezels, and the introduction of OLED display technology. This round of intensive updates is part of Apple’s broader product roadmap. According to Bloomberg, Apple also plans to launch refreshed versions of the MacBook Neo and MacBook Air in the first half of next year, aside from the touchscreen MacBook Pro. On the chip roadmap, Apple is expected to release the M7, M7 Pro, and M7 Max chips in 2027, along with a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro; the M7 Ultra chip and a new Mac Studio are scheduled for release in 2028. Apple is continuing its comprehensive overhaul of its computer lineup to meet growing demands for artificial intelligence applications; the two new products released today are milestones in this journey, not the final destination.

Two new models will be available for pre-order at 1:10 AM on October 29, with official shipping beginning on November 6. The new iMac starts at RMB 12,499, and the MacBook Pro starts at RMB 15,999. Apple stated that the M6 chip enables the new iMac to deliver five times the performance on AI tasks compared to the previous generation, while the entry-level MacBook Pro offers a 30% improvement in graphics processing over its predecessor. This release is the second wave of Apple’s product launch campaign this week. On Monday, the company updated the iPad mini with an upgraded display and water-resistant features. Wall Street Journal noted that Apple will conclude its product releases this week on Wednesday with its first-ever touchscreen MacBook Pro. The new iMac and MacBook Pro closely resemble their predecessors in design, with main changes focused on internal hardware. Both models feature the M6 chip—first introduced in September alongside the Mac mini. In this update, the iMac has jumped from the M4 chip to the M6 chip, while the MacBook Pro only received the M5 chip last year, resulting in a relatively shorter iteration cycle. In terms of connectivity, both new devices support Bluetooth 6 and Wi-Fi 7, and the new MacBook Pro also features faster charging. Apple continues to sell the high-end MacBook Pro models equipped with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, both of which feature higher specifications for the main processor and graphics cores compared to the newly released entry-level M6 model. Apple will release its first MacBook Pro with a touchscreen this Wednesday, ending the company’s two-decade-long resistance to touchscreens on laptops. The new touch-screen MacBook Pro will feature a lighter and thinner design, narrower screen bezels, and the introduction of OLED display technology. This round of intensive updates is part of Apple’s broader product roadmap. According to Bloomberg, Apple also plans to launch refreshed versions of the MacBook Neo and MacBook Air in the first half of next year, aside from the touchscreen MacBook Pro. On the chip roadmap, Apple is expected to release the M7, M7 Pro, and M7 Max chips in 2027, along with a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro; the M7 Ultra chip and a new Mac Studio are scheduled for release in 2028. Apple is continuing its comprehensive overhaul of its computer lineup to meet growing demands for artificial intelligence applications; the two new products released today are milestones in this journey, not the final destination.

sources.title: Apple launches the M6-powered iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro: key upgrades, features and what changes
passages: Apple has unveiled a refreshed 24-inch iMac and an entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro, both powered by its new M6 chip, as the company continues to update its Mac lineup.
The launches also come ahead of anticipated changes to Apple's higher-end MacBook Pro range, which has been linked to a potential touchscreen display and other hardware improvements.
AI capabilities remain a key focusThe M6-powered models reflect Apple's continued emphasis on improving performance while expanding the capabilities of on-device AI.
The iMac offers a fixed desktop setup, while the MacBook Pro provides a portable option for users who need performance on the move.
By introducing the M6 chip across both desktop and laptop models, Apple is extending its latest processor generation to customers with different computing requirements.
Apple's decision to retain familiar designs means the latest models are primarily hardware updates.
The upgrades focus primarily on performance, power efficiency and artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities rather than a major redesign of either device.

extraction.body: Apple has unveiled a refreshed 24-inch iMac and an entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro, both powered by its new M6 chip, as the company continues to update its Mac lineup. Announced on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the launches bring processor upgrades to two of Apple's core computer offerings while retaining the designs of their predecessors. The updated iMac succeeds the previous M4-powered model, while the base 14-inch MacBook Pro moves on from the M5 chip introduced last year. The upgrades focus primarily on performance, power efficiency and artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities rather than a major redesign of either device. The launches also come ahead of anticipated changes to Apple's higher-end MacBook Pro range, which has been linked to a potential touchscreen display and other hardware improvements. Apple iMac, MacBook Pro get M6 chip upgradeThe new M6 chip is central to both launches, bringing Apple's latest silicon to its all-in-one desktop and entry-level professional laptop. The processor is expected to deliver faster computing performance and enhanced AI capabilities, supporting Apple's broader focus on running more intelligence-related tasks directly on its devices. For the 24-inch iMac, the upgrade replaces the M4 processor found in the previous generation. The desktop continues with its colourful all-in-one design, combining the computer's hardware and display in a single unit. The entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro also retains its existing form factor, with the M6 replacing the M5 chip used in the previous generation. The model targets users who want the MacBook Pro range's performance and features without opting for higher-end configurations. Apple's decision to retain familiar designs means the latest models are primarily hardware updates. The company has not introduced a substantial exterior redesign as part of these launches. AI capabilities remain a key focusThe M6-powered models reflect Apple's continued emphasis on improving performance while expanding the capabilities of on-device AI. By introducing the M6 chip across both desktop and laptop models, Apple is extending its latest processor generation to customers with different computing requirements. The iMac offers a fixed desktop setup, while the MacBook Pro provides a portable option for users who need performance on the move. However, detailed performance comparisons, configuration-specific specifications and real-world benchmarks would be needed to establish the extent of the improvements over the previous M4 and M5 models. Touchscreen MacBook Pro could be the next major updateThe launches come as attention builds around anticipated changes to Apple's higher-end MacBook Pro lineup. Future models have been linked to touchscreen functionality and potential display advances, although these developments should be treated as expected changes rather than confirmed features of the newly announced devices. For now, the M6-powered iMac and entry-level MacBook Pro represent incremental updates to Apple's existing computer range. The new processors bring the latest silicon to two established product categories while leaving their familiar designs intact.

extraction.body: Personally identifiable information belonging to thousands of U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees has been published online after a hacker stole reams of data in a previously undisclosed breach at the government department earlier this year. The breach includes names, job titles, and work contact information, such as email addresses, cell phone numbers, and office locations, of more than 40,000 people who work for the federal department, including border and immigration agents, cybersecurity staffers, and senior department officials. A hacker who goes by the handle Department of Peace claimed they obtained the data from an Okta single sign-on system used by Homeland Security to allow employees and contractors across its various agencies to log in to its central network. The Okta system also contains IT and log-in records associated with the employees’ user account, including details about which systems and internal apps they are permitted to access. More than half of the dataset — some 21,000 records — relate to employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), who work at airports and other ports of entry. The data also contains records associated with another 10,000 employees of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) unit, and just under a 1,000 employees who work at U.S. cybersecurity defense agency CISA. Thousands of additional records relate to staff who work at the department’s headquarters and its other agencies, including U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and the Federal Protective Service. “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” said Department of Peace in a note left with the data, which TechCrunch has seen. The hacker did not respond to TechCrunch’s email requesting comment and with questions about how the breach was carried out. This is the latest data breach to hit the U.S. government in recent months, following earlier hacks involving the theft of thousands of FBI agents’ personnel records and the personal information of millions of serving and former military service personnel from the Pentagon’s human resources unit . It’s also the second breach involving Homeland Security this year, after the same hacker claimed to have taken thousands of contracts between the department and the private sector, including defense contractors and surveillance vendors. The latest batch of breached data, which appears authentic, offers a rare — albeit incomplete — view into the scale and operations of Homeland Security, whose deportations, arbitrary detentions, and killings of U.S. citizens under its leadership have become a key issue for voters ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections. The stolen Homeland Security data was provided to journalist and hacker maia arson crimew, who then shared a copy with DDoSecrets , a nonprofit collective that hosts leaked datasets in the public interest. TechCrunch verified a portion of the data as authentic by matching the names of several known Homeland Security employees against an offline copy of the database. The thousands of employee directory records appear to have been exfiltrated around mid-August, according to the timestamps on each person’s record. The number of leaked records is equivalent to about one-fifth of Homeland Security’s workforce, which totals around 220,000 staff . It’s unclear whether the vulnerability that allowed the breach has been fixed or if Homeland Security is aware of the data theft. A spokesperson for Homeland Security did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment about the breach. When reached, Okta said it was aware of this report. “Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” a spokesperson said. While the leaked data includes identifiable information about agents and officers, the dataset also reveals more about the surveillance technologies and cybersecurity tools that Homeland Security employees may be able to access. Critics have called for investigations into tech companies that fund or provide their technology to ICE. The leaked data contains information about employees’ membership in user groups within the department’s Active Directory, a system that controls access to the department’s internal tools, services, and third-party offerings used for work. Most of the Homeland Security employees in the dataset were members of the user group that had access to Microsoft 365, the tech giant’s cloud service that hosts the agency’s emails and files, as well as user groups for accessing Adobe Acrobat, Citrix, and other typical desktop software. The data also shows that around 4,500 users, including ICE agents and deportation officers, are members of a group called “Headspace_users.” Online therapy provider Headspace previously had an $82,500 federal contract with ICE that ended in 2023 to fund “mental health software required for ERO employees,” a reference to ICE’s deportation unit. A spokesperson for Headspace said the company has not provided any services to DHS or ICE since 2023. Dozens of other user groups reference Penlink , a web surveillance company that makes technology it claims can track the location data of hundreds of millions of mobile devices. Penlink has had a contract with ICE for years. The user groups vary in size, from a handful of users in local Homeland Security offices around the country to more than 2,000 users across ICE’s HSI unit nationally. One group specifically references Penlink PLX, which the company says is used to capture and analyze “real-time intelligence” from phone calls, texts, web activity, and social media. A spokesperson for Penlink did not respond to a request for comment. One user group also includes more than 200 CBP users associated with Mobile Fortify, a facial-recognition app used by both CBP and ICE agents to identify people and verify their information and immigration status . The user groups also include several employees associated with ChatGPT access, including senior DHS officials, as well as other groups associated with investigations into the China-backed hacking groups known as Salt Typhoon and Volt Typhoon. Researchers and public information advocates say that the exposed data could provide valuable leads for investigations into alleged abuses by the Trump administration, such as identifying email addresses of agents that can be used in public records requests under the Freedom of Information Act. “Email addresses and phone numbers are indispensable tools for FOIA researchers, often making the difference between a vague records request that gets stonewalled and one that gets results,” said Ryan Shapiro, the executive director of transparency nonprofit Property of the People. “Given the Trump administration’s contempt for even basic transparency, the need for such tools is urgent,” said Shapiro. DDoSecrets co-founder and journalist Emma Best said that the exposed Homeland Security data will be a “catalyst for investigations, empowering journalists, Congressional inquiries, legal challenges, community action and Freedom of Information Act requests.” Zack Whittaker is the security editor at TechCrunch. He also authors the weekly cybersecurity newsletter, this week in security . He can be reached via encrypted message at zackwhittaker.1337 on Signal. You can also contact him by email, or to verify outreach, at [email protected] .

The stolen Homeland Security data was provided to journalist and hacker maia arson crimew, who then shared a copy with DDoSecrets , a nonprofit collective that hosts leaked datasets in the public interest.

TechCrunch verified a portion of the data as authentic by matching the names of several known Homeland Security employees against an offline copy of the database. The thousands of employee directory records appear to have been exfiltrated around mid-August, according to the timestamps on each person’s record. The number of leaked records is equivalent to about one-fifth of Homeland Security’s workforce, which totals around 220,000 staff .
It’s unclear whether the vulnerability that allowed the breach has been fixed or if Homeland Security is aware of the data theft.
A spokesperson for Homeland Security did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment about the breach.
When reached, Okta said it was aware of this report. “Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” a spokesperson said.

While the leaked data includes identifiable information about agents and officers, the dataset also reveals more about the surveillance technologies and cybersecurity tools that Homeland Security employees may be able to access. Critics have called for investigations into tech companies that fund or provide their technology to ICE.

The leaked data contains information about employees’ membership in user groups within the department’s Active Directory, a system that controls access to the department’s internal tools, services, and third-party offerings used for work.

Most of the Homeland Security employees in the dataset were members of the user group that had access to Microsoft 365, the tech giant’s cloud service that hosts the agency’s emails and files, as well as user groups for accessing Adobe Acrobat, Citrix, and other typical desktop software.

The data also shows that around 4,500 users, including ICE agents and deportation officers, are members of a group called “Headspace_users.” Online therapy provider Headspace previously had an $82,500 federal contract with ICE that ended in 2023 to fund “mental health software required for ERO employees,” a reference to ICE’s deportation unit.
A spokesperson for Headspace said the company has not provided any services to DHS or ICE since 2023.

Dozens of other user groups reference Penlink , a web surveillance company that makes technology it claims can track the location data of hundreds of millions of mobile devices. Penlink has had a contract with ICE for years. The user groups vary in size, from a handful of users in local Homeland Security offices around the country to more than 2,000 users across ICE’s HSI unit nationally. One group specifically references Penlink PLX, which the company says is used to capture and analyze “real-time intelligence” from phone calls, texts, web activity, and social media.
A spokesperson for Penlink did not respond to a request for comment.

One user group also includes more than 200 CBP users associated with Mobile Fortify, a facial-recognition app used by both CBP and ICE agents to identify people and verify their information and immigration status .

The user groups also include several employees associated with ChatGPT access, including senior DHS officials, as well as other groups associated with investigations into the China-backed hacking groups known as Salt Typhoon and Volt Typhoon.

Researchers and public information advocates say that the exposed data could provide valuable leads for investigations into alleged abuses by the Trump administration, such as identifying email addresses of agents that can be used in public records requests under the Freedom of Information Act.

“Email addresses and phone numbers are indispensable tools for FOIA researchers, often making the difference between a vague records request that gets stonewalled and one that gets results,” said Ryan Shapiro, the executive director of transparency nonprofit Property of the People.
“Given the Trump administration’s contempt for even basic transparency, the need for such tools is urgent,” said Shapiro.

DDoSecrets co-founder and journalist Emma Best said that the exposed Homeland Security data will be a “catalyst for investigations, empowering journalists, Congressional inquiries, legal challenges, community action and Freedom of Information Act requests.”
Zack Whittaker is the security editor at TechCrunch. He also authors the weekly cybersecurity newsletter, this week in security .

passages: Personally identifiable information belonging to thousands of U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees has been published online after a hacker stole reams of data in a previously undisclosed breach at the government department earlier this year.

The breach includes names, job titles, and work contact information, such as email addresses, cell phone numbers, and office locations, of more than 40,000 people who work for the federal department, including border and immigration agents, cybersecurity staffers, and senior department officials.

A hacker who goes by the handle Department of Peace claimed they obtained the data from an Okta single sign-on system used by Homeland Security to allow employees and contractors across its various agencies to log in to its central network. The Okta system also contains IT and log-in records associated with the employees’ user account, including details about which systems and internal apps they are permitted to access.
More than half of the dataset — some 21,000 records — relate to employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), who work at airports and other ports of entry.

The data also contains records associated with another 10,000 employees of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) unit, and just under a 1,000 employees who work at U.S. cybersecurity defense agency CISA.

Thousands of additional records relate to staff who work at the department’s headquarters and its other agencies, including U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and the Federal Protective Service.

“They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” said Department of Peace in a note left with the data, which TechCrunch has seen. The hacker did not respond to TechCrunch’s email requesting comment and with questions about how the breach was carried out.

This is the latest data breach to hit the U.S. government in recent months, following earlier hacks involving the theft of thousands of FBI agents’ personnel records and the personal information of millions of serving and former military service personnel from the Pentagon’s human resources unit . It’s also the second breach involving Homeland Security this year, after the same hacker claimed to have taken thousands of contracts between the department and the private sector, including defense contractors and surveillance vendors.

The latest batch of breached data, which appears authentic, offers a rare — albeit incomplete — view into the scale and operations of Homeland Security, whose deportations, arbitrary detentions, and killings of U.S. citizens under its leadership have become a key issue for voters ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections.

The stolen Homeland Security data was provided to journalist and hacker maia arson crimew, who then shared a copy with DDoSecrets , a nonprofit collective that hosts leaked datasets in the public interest.

TechCrunch verified a portion of the data as authentic by matching the names of several known Homeland Security employees against an offline copy of the database. The thousands of employee directory records appear to have been exfiltrated around mid-August, according to the timestamps on each person’s record. The number of leaked records is equivalent to about one-fifth of Homeland Security’s workforce, which totals around 220,000 staff .
It’s unclear whether the vulnerability that allowed the breach has been fixed or if Homeland Security is aware of the data theft.
A spokesperson for Homeland Security did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment about the breach.
When reached, Okta said it was aware of this report. “Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised,” a spokesperson said.

While the leaked data includes identifiable information about agents and officers, the dataset also reveals more about the surveillance technologies and cybersecurity tools that Homeland Security employees may be able to access. Critics have called for investigations into tech companies that fund or provide their technology to ICE.

The leaked data contains information about employees’ membership in user groups within the department’s Active Directory, a system that controls access to the department’s internal tools, services, and third-party offerings used for work.

Most of the Homeland Security employees in the dataset were members of the user group that had access to Microsoft 365, the tech giant’s cloud service that hosts the agency’s emails and files, as well as user groups for accessing Adobe Acrobat, Citrix, and other typical desktop software.

The data also shows that around 4,500 users, including ICE agents and deportation officers, are members of a group called “Headspace_users.” Online therapy provider Headspace previously had an $82,500 federal contract with ICE that ended in 2023 to fund “mental health software required for ERO employees,” a reference to ICE’s deportation unit.
A spokesperson for Headspace said the company has not provided any services to DHS or ICE since 2023.

Dozens of other user groups reference Penlink , a web surveillance company that makes technology it claims can track the location data of hundreds of millions of mobile devices. Penlink has had a contract with ICE for years. The user groups vary in size, from a handful of users in local Homeland Security offices around the country to more than 2,000 users across ICE’s HSI unit nationally. One group specifically references Penlink PLX, which the company says is used to capture and analyze “real-time intelligence” from phone calls, texts, web activity, and social media.
A spokesperson for Penlink did not respond to a request for comment.

One user group also includes more than 200 CBP users associated with Mobile Fortify, a facial-recognition app used by both CBP and ICE agents to identify people and verify their information and immigration status .

The user groups also include several employees associated with ChatGPT access, including senior DHS officials, as well as other groups associated with investigations into the China-backed hacking groups known as Salt Typhoon and Volt Typhoon.

Researchers and public information advocates say that the exposed data could provide valuable leads for investigations into alleged abuses by the Trump administration, such as identifying email addresses of agents that can be used in public records requests under the Freedom of Information Act.

“Email addresses and phone numbers are indispensable tools for FOIA researchers, often making the difference between a vague records request that gets stonewalled and one that gets results,” said Ryan Shapiro, the executive director of transparency nonprofit Property of the People.
“Given the Trump administration’s contempt for even basic transparency, the need for such tools is urgent,” said Shapiro.

DDoSecrets co-founder and journalist Emma Best said that the exposed Homeland Security data will be a “catalyst for investigations, empowering journalists, Congressional inquiries, legal challenges, community action and Freedom of Information Act requests.”
Zack Whittaker is the security editor at TechCrunch. He also authors the weekly cybersecurity newsletter, this week in security .
He can be reached via encrypted message at zackwhittaker.1337 on Signal. You can also contact him by email, or to verify outreach, at [email protected] .

sources.title: Apple Touchscreen MacBook Pro: $2,899, Nov. 6 [2026] - shattered.io
passages: Apple announced its first touchscreen laptop on October 28, 2026, and the price tag landed as loudly as the feature.
The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch, according to Ars Technica’s launch coverage .
Both sizes use Apple’s M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, and both go on sale November 6, 2026.
The gap between the two sizes is exactly $500, or roughly 17% on top of the smaller model’s base price.
Apple has not published a wider configuration list in the material we verified, so those two numbers are the only prices we can state with confidence.
The takeaway: Apple has crossed a line it held for years, and it did so at the top of its price range.
Whether that bet works depends on facts the company has not yet shown, from battery life to repair costs to how well macOS handles fingers.

This analysis covers what Apple confirmed, what it left open, how the pricing compares with the rest of the market, and what the touchscreen MacBook Pro means for buyers, developers and rival laptop makers.
BNN Bloomberg’s report on the first touchscreen laptops arriving amid a product blitz placed the launch inside a busy stretch for Apple, and that context matters for pricing.
When a company launches several products in a short window, it usually prices the newest halo item high and lets cheaper models absorb the volume.
A $2,899 entry point reads as a halo price, aimed at buyers who already pay for top-end Pro hardware.
Retailers and resellers face a trickier picture.
Investors will watch the November 6 launch window and the following quarter for signs of whether premium Mac demand holds.
We will track the broader hardware picture in our hardware coverage hub as sales data arrives.
For now, the sensible stance is interest without haste.
Past launches, from the first Retina MacBook Pro to the mini-LED displays, followed a similar path.
Coverage names John Ternus as the Apple executive who unveiled the touchscreen MacBooks, and identifies him as the company’s CEO.
OLED panels draw different power than LCD panels depending on what is on screen, and a touch layer adds its own overhead.
If you plan to buy on November 6, wait for reviews that run the same workload on the old and new models.
Pricing tells you who Apple expects to buy first.
The gaps in the announcement are as useful to know as the specs.
Several details that buyers will want before spending $2,899 or more are not in the verified record.
We list them here so readers do not mistake rumor for fact.

The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch, according to Ars Technica’s launch coverage . Both sizes use Apple’s M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, and both go on sale November 6, 2026. For a company that spent more than a decade steering Mac owners toward the keyboard and trackpad, this is a real reversal. We tracked the build-up in our earlier look at the Pro and tell launch expectations , and the final product matches the broad outline. This analysis covers what Apple confirmed, what it left open, how the pricing compares with the rest of the market, and what the touchscreen MacBook Pro means for buyers, developers and rival laptop makers. Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. Apple calls the product the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, and coverage identifies it as the company’s first laptop with a touch-sensitive screen. It ships in two sizes, 14 inches and 16 inches. Apple’s M5 Pro and M5 Max chips power the lineup. The company showed the machines at its “Pro and tell” event, where John Ternus, identified in coverage as Apple’s CEO, unveiled the touchscreen MacBooks. The headline feature is simple to state. You can now touch the Mac’s screen and expect it to respond. The harder question is what that changes in daily use. Apple has not turned the MacBook Pro into a tablet. The hardware stays a clamshell laptop with a keyboard and trackpad, and the touch layer sits on top of the existing Mac experience. How deeply macOS adapts to fingers, and which apps get touch-native controls on day one, remain open points that the announcement coverage does not settle. The Verge published the reveal video for the touchscreen MacBook Pro , which gives the clearest first look at how Apple chose to present the change. CNN Business framed the news more bluntly, with a headline that called it Apple’s first-ever MacBook with a touchscreen. Reuters, Ars Technica and other outlets reached the same conclusion. The story is not that Apple copied a Windows feature. The story is that Apple moved at all. Three facts anchor everything else in this piece. First, the display technology is new to the MacBook Pro line. Second, the price floor sits well above where most people expect a laptop to start. Third, the on-sale date is only nine days away, so Apple has little time to let rumor fill the gaps. Those three facts shape the rest of the analysis below. The 14-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $2,899. The 16-inch starts at $3,399. The gap between the two sizes is exactly $500, or roughly 17% on top of the smaller model’s base price. Apple has not published a wider configuration list in the material we verified, so those two numbers are the only prices we can state with confidence. passages: While September is the traditional time for Apple's iPhone event, reliable sources are indicating that we will NOT be seeing the introduction of the iPhone 12 lineup at next week's event.
Instead, the event with a tagline of "Time Flies" will be largely focused on new Apple Watch and iPad models .
Check out our complete look at what we expect to see at the event for more details.
This week also saw new rumors about iPhone 12 launch plans, new developments in the dispute between Apple and Epic Games, and a rumor about the chip destined for the first Apple Silicon-based Mac.
Apple has said the new iPhones will be launching "a few weeks later" than usual, so another event in early October seems likely.
MacRumors attracts a broad audience of both consumers and professionals interested in the latest technologies and products.
But even then, word is that the four new iPhone 12 models will see a staggered launch due to supply constraints.
Epic says it is "likely to suffer irreparable harm" if Fortnite is kept off of the App Store.
For its part, Apple says that the situation is of Epic's own making, and Apple has filed a countersuit for breach of contract damages.
Apple says Epic engaged in "willful, brazen, and unlawful conduct" in what amounts to "nothing more than a basic disagreement over money."
Whether you're upgrading from an older iPhone or completely new to Apple, this guide will help you get the most out your new device.
Regardless of the exact timing, carriers are starting to ramp up preparations for the launch, and Apple is said to be starting mass production on the new models later this month .
Apple is famous for disguising its prototype devices to make it more difficult to identify them, and some new photos reveal the lengths Apple went to in hiding the Apple Watch before its debut .
