Google today opened a preview of its Connected Apps Platform, a single route for outside developers to build their services into both Google Search and the Gemini app. The announcement, posted on Google's blog by Chips Mistry, Group Product Manager for Search, and Mai Lowe, Group Product Manager for the Gemini app, introduces a Google Connected Console where developers register, test and submit apps for review, and choose which of the two products each app appears in. Google also said it has now launched more than 50 Connected Apps across Search and Gemini, naming Adobe, Calm, Experian, Localiza and Peloton among its partners. Access is opening in phases, and the post gives no fees, no list of markets and no account of how Google decides which app handles a request.

Google is letting more companies build their apps into Google Search and the Gemini assistant, so people can do things like book a table or plan a workout without leaving Google. That matters to any business with an app, because these connected apps are the ones Search and Gemini can hand a task to when someone asks for help. For now it is a preview that opens in stages, and Google has not said what it costs, how it picks between competing apps, or what user data changes hands.

The post is short. Dated October 28, 2026, carrying a three-minute read time and filed under Developer tools, Search and Gemini App, it runs to five paragraphs under the headline "Build and manage Connected Apps in one place." Two announcements share the space: a developer platform, and a new set of consumer integrations.

On the first, the wording is direct. "To help users get more done, today we're launching the preview of our Connected Apps Platform, a unified way for more app developers to bring their capabilities directly into Gemini and Search," according to the post. Google frames the platform as a consolidation, describing it in the summary line as "a single place to build and manage apps for Search and the Gemini app."

The operative word is preview. "We're opening access in phases, and will add more developers, markets, and Google products over the coming months," the post states, pointing developers to a sign-up and documentation at developers.google.com/connected-apps. The announcement does not say how many developers are admitted in the first phase, which countries or languages are covered, or when the preview ends. The reference to adding "Google products" in the plural suggests the platform is meant to reach beyond Search and Gemini at some point, though the post names no other product.

The technical description fits in a single sentence. "Developers integrate with a cloud-hosted MCP server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, then use the Google Connected Console to register, test, and submit their app," according to Google.

Both routes rest on the Model Context Protocol , the open standard Anthropic introduced in November 2024 for connecting AI models to outside tools and data. An MCP server publishes a list of "tools" - discrete actions such as searching inventory, checking availability or placing a booking - which an AI model can call on a user's behalf. Google's platform accepts that standard rather than asking developers to adopt a proprietary format, which in principle lets a company reuse a server it already runs for other AI assistants.
That sequence places Google as a gatekeeper. Nothing goes live without review, though the developer, not Google, decides the publishing moment once approval is granted.

One decision is made before review. "Before review, developers choose whether it will go live in Search, the Gemini app, or both," according to the post. The pitch to developers is that a single build covers both. The platform, Google says, "gives developers the opportunity to build once and reach high-intent users across both Search and the Gemini app." No figure accompanies "high-intent," and the post does not say how many people use Connected Apps today.

After launch, the reporting is operational. "Once live, you can track traffic, latency, and error rates, and keep control of your brand identity, including verified logos and authenticated accounts," the post states. Traffic, latency and error rates are the measures an engineering team watches to keep a service running. The post mentions no conversion data, no revenue reporting and no visibility into which user requests triggered an app.

The second half of the post concerns the apps users can reach. "We've launched more than 50 Connected Apps between Search and Gemini in areas ranging from productivity and event ticketing to health and fitness," according to Google.

Four partners are singled out. "Integrations with partners like Adobe, Experian, Localiza, and Peloton are live for users in Gemini, and in the coming weeks, we'll be bringing these Connected Apps to Search as well," the post states. Localiza is a Brazilian car rental company; the post does not describe what its integration does or in which markets it is available. The fifth name is new across both products: "Among other apps, we'll also be launching a new integration with Calm across both Search and Gemini."

For three of the four Gemini names, the news today is Search. Adobe, Experian and Peloton were among the 14 connected apps Google began rolling out in Gemini on September 23 , a batch that also included Airtable, Linear, monday.com, Squarespace and Webflow. Adobe's tools from Photoshop, Lightroom, Express and Firefly began a global rollout inside Gemini on September 24 .

The "more than 50" figure is harder to place. PPC Land reported on August 12 that Google's own availability help article already listed 41 connected apps before that day's batch of 13 named partners, five of which were already on the list. Fourteen more followed in September. On October 13, Google said the Gemini app connects to "more than 40 apps" . Today's post counts Search and Gemini together. It does not say whether an app available in both products is counted once or twice, and the arithmetic from Google's earlier lists points to a total for Gemini alone that is already above 50. Google directs readers to its help center pages for Search and Gemini for the complete list.
Several questions that matter to anyone weighing an integration go unanswered in the announcement.
Economics. There is no mention of fees, revenue share or charges to developers, and nothing on whether users pay to reach any app beyond what the partner itself charges.

Selection. When two ticketing apps or two fitness apps are both connected, which one does Search or Gemini call? The post does not describe how a request is routed, whether users must link an app before it can be used, or whether Google may suggest an app the user has not connected. For brands, that routing logic plays the role ranking plays in search results.

Data. "Authenticated accounts" implies that users sign in to a partner service through Google, but the post does not describe the linking process, what user information passes from Google to the developer, what returns to Google, or how long either side keeps it.

Connected apps change what an AI answer can do: instead of linking to a business, Search or Gemini can call the business's service directly. When Google first brought Instacart, Canva and YouTube Music into AI Mode in Search on July 16 , AI Mode assembled a task and then sent the user to the partner to finish it. Until now, which companies got that treatment was decided through partnerships announced in batches. A console with a submission queue turns it into something closer to an application process, even if Google keeps the final say through review.

The audience on the Gemini side is large. Alphabet reported on July 22 that the Gemini app had reached 950 million monthly users . That app carries no advertising. Google's vice president of global ads, Dan Taylor, denied in December 2025 that ads were coming to Gemini , and in January said there were no plans for ads in the Gemini app . With no paid placement on offer, being a connected app is one of the few ways a brand can be present inside Gemini's interface at the moment a user asks for something it sells.

The single build for two surfaces also fits what Google's leadership has been saying in public. Sundar Pichai, speaking on the Sources podcast on October 21, said agents rather than a merger of products would unify Search and Gemini . A developer registering once and switching on either product, or both, is that idea expressed as tooling.

Measurement remains the gap. The console's metrics - traffic, latency and error rates - tell an engineering team whether the integration works. They do not tell a marketing team whether a booking made inside Gemini came from a campaign, a brand search or nothing at all. Neither the post nor the console view Google published shows any link to Google Ads, Google Analytics or conversion tracking.

Brand control gets one line. Verified logos and authenticated accounts address a real risk in an open submission system: an app that looks like a well-known brand but is not. The post does not say how verification works or what proof a developer must provide.

Commerce is running on a parallel track. On October 15, Google began rolling out Universal Cart across US Search and the Gemini app , a cross-retailer basket that hands checkout to Google Pay or the merchant's site. Merchants reach shoppers through one system, and service apps such as fitness, ticketing or car rental now through another.

The decision to build the platform on MCP follows more than a year of Google adopting the protocol piece by piece. On July 7, 2025, Google said it was exploring an MCP server for the Google Ads API , and on October 7, 2025, it released an open-source version . In February 2026, the Chrome team proposed WebMCP, which would let websites offer structured tools to agents instead of leaving them to screenshot analysis, page parsing and simulated clicks . The Gemini app gained custom MCP connections in its June 30 update , the same release that added Instacart and OpenTable as connected apps.

Today's platform moves MCP from a setting that individual users configure to the formal entry point for companies. Users connecting their own servers is one thing; Google reviewing, publishing and monitoring third-party servers across its two largest AI surfaces is another.

Google is not alone in that direction. Meta's Developer Tools MCP launched on June 30, letting developers manage Meta apps through AI assistants, and on April 29 Meta opened Ads AI Connectors that let Claude and ChatGPT create and edit campaigns . The protocol is becoming the common plumbing of agentic AI , with each platform deciding who gets to plug in and on what terms. Google's terms, for now, are a sign-up form and a review queue.

Who: Google, through a post by Chips Mistry, Group Product Manager for Search, and Mai Lowe, Group Product Manager for the Gemini app. App developers are the intended users of the new platform, with Adobe, Calm, Experian, Localiza and Peloton named as Connected Apps partners.

What: A preview of the Connected Apps Platform, which lets developers connect a cloud-hosted MCP server or an Android MCP integration built on the AppFunctions APIs, then register, test and submit the app through a new Google Connected Console. Developers choose Search, the Gemini app or both before Google reviews the app, and can track traffic, latency and error rates once it is live. Google says more than 50 Connected Apps are now live across the two products.

When: Announced today, October 28, 2026. Access opens in phases over the coming months; Adobe, Experian, Localiza and Peloton are due to reach Search in the coming weeks, and Calm is launching on both products.
Where: Google Search and the Gemini app. The post names no countries or languages for the preview and says more markets and Google products will be added.

Why: Google says the platform lets developers "build once and reach high-intent users across both Search and the Gemini app." For marketers, it opens a formal route for brands to put their services inside Google's AI surfaces, including a Gemini app that carries no ads, while leaving fees, app selection, data sharing and conversion measurement unaddressed.

extraction.body: Google is making it easier for businesses to connect their apps to its AI experiences across Search and Gemini with the debut of its Connected Apps Platform. Introduced in Gemini and Google Search earlier this year, connected apps let users securely link and interact with popular third-party services, then use them to take specific actions. For instance, you could connect to Canva to design a flyer, or to YouTube Music to build a playlist. We’ve seen varying takes on the idea by other consumer-facing AI services like ChatGPT and Meta’s Muse. The premise is that such integrations could ultimately shift consumer behavior away from launching and using individual apps to instead using their favorite services through their preferred AI provider. However, to successfully capture and retain consumers’ attention, there have to actually be a wide range of connected apps to explore. Google’s idea is to open its doors to any business or developer that wants to reach users through Search or Gemini by allowing them to submit their own connected apps and monitor their performance. The platform preview is currently available in beta to developers in the U.S., and will allow developers to build and submit apps that can be used across Google’s products. To get started, developers would integrate with a cloud-hosted MCP (Model Context Protocol) server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, then use the Google Connected Console to register, test, and submit their app, Google explains. Essentially, this process lets devs connect their app to Google’s services so it can be used with the search giant’s AI features. Developers can also choose whether they want their app to be available via Search, the Gemini app, or both. After the app is live, developers can track traffic, latency, and error rates, and maintain control over their brand identity, such as their verified logos and authenticated accounts. Similar to how SEO allowed companies and websites to show search engine rankings, this could well be one of the initial steps for businesses that want their services to be more visible to users on the agentic web. Google already has over 50 Connected Apps available in Gemini, including from partners like Adobe, Experian, Localiza, Peloton, and others, in addition to its own expansive set of services, from Workplace and Photos to YouTube Music and Google Home. These apps will now come to Google Search over the next few weeks. Search today has fewer integrations, featuring apps like Instacart, Canva, YouTube Music, Yahoo Fantasy Football, and others. Google said meditation app Calm is another new partner on this effort, and that its app will soon launch on both Gemini and Search. The new Connected Apps platform is in public preview for U.S. developers who sign up for the waitlist. Google did not share when it would become more broadly available. Google today opened a preview of its Connected Apps Platform, a single route for outside developers to build their services into both Google Search and the Gemini app. The announcement, posted on Google's blog by Chips Mistry, Group Product Manager for Search, and Mai Lowe, Group Product Manager for the Gemini app, introduces a Google Connected Console where developers register, test and submit apps for review, and choose which of the two products each app appears in. Google also said it has now launched more than 50 Connected Apps across Search and Gemini, naming Adobe, Calm, Experian, Localiza and Peloton among its partners. Access is opening in phases, and the post gives no fees, no list of markets and no account of how Google decides which app handles a request. Google is letting more companies build their apps into Google Search and the Gemini assistant, so people can do things like book a table or plan a workout without leaving Google. That matters to any business with an app, because these connected apps are the ones Search and Gemini can hand a task to when someone asks for help. For now it is a preview that opens in stages, and Google has not said what it costs, how it picks between competing apps, or what user data changes hands. The post is short. Dated October 28, 2026, carrying a three-minute read time and filed under Developer tools, Search and Gemini App, it runs to five paragraphs under the headline "Build and manage Connected Apps in one place." Two announcements share the space: a developer platform, and a new set of consumer integrations. On the first, the wording is direct. "To help users get more done, today we're launching the preview of our Connected Apps Platform, a unified way for more app developers to bring their capabilities directly into Gemini and Search," according to the post. Google frames the platform as a consolidation, describing it in the summary line as "a single place to build and manage apps for Search and the Gemini app." The operative word is preview. "We're opening access in phases, and will add more developers, markets, and Google products over the coming months," the post states, pointing developers to a sign-up and documentation at developers.google.com/connected-apps. The announcement does not say how many developers are admitted in the first phase, which countries or languages are covered, or when the preview ends. The reference to adding "Google products" in the plural suggests the platform is meant to reach beyond Search and Gemini at some point, though the post names no other product. The technical description fits in a single sentence. "Developers integrate with a cloud-hosted MCP server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, then use the Google Connected Console to register, test, and submit their app," according to Google. Both routes rest on the Model Context Protocol , the open standard Anthropic introduced in November 2024 for connecting AI models to outside tools and data. An MCP server publishes a list of "tools" - discrete actions such as searching inventory, checking availability or placing a booking - which an AI model can call on a user's behalf. Google's platform accepts that standard rather than asking developers to adopt a proprietary format, which in principle lets a company reuse a server it already runs for other AI assistants. That sequence places Google as a gatekeeper. Nothing goes live without review, though the developer, not Google, decides the publishing moment once approval is granted. One decision is made before review. "Before review, developers choose whether it will go live in Search, the Gemini app, or both," according to the post. The pitch to developers is that a single build covers both. The platform, Google says, "gives developers the opportunity to build once and reach high-intent users across both Search and the Gemini app." No figure accompanies "high-intent," and the post does not say how many people use Connected Apps today. After launch, the reporting is operational. "Once live, you can track traffic, latency, and error rates, and keep control of your brand identity, including verified logos and authenticated accounts," the post states. Traffic, latency and error rates are the measures an engineering team watches to keep a service running. The post mentions no conversion data, no revenue reporting and no visibility into which user requests triggered an app. The second half of the post concerns the apps users can reach. "We've launched more than 50 Connected Apps between Search and Gemini in areas ranging from productivity and event ticketing to health and fitness," according to Google. Four partners are singled out. "Integrations with partners like Adobe, Experian, Localiza, and Peloton are live for users in Gemini, and in the coming weeks, we'll be bringing these Connected Apps to Search as well," the post states. Localiza is a Brazilian car rental company; the post does not describe what its integration does or in which markets it is available. The fifth name is new across both products: "Among other apps, we'll also be launching a new integration with Calm across both Search and Gemini." For three of the four Gemini names, the news today is Search. Adobe, Experian and Peloton were among the 14 connected apps Google began rolling out in Gemini on September 23 , a batch that also included Airtable, Linear, monday.com, Squarespace and Webflow. Adobe's tools from Photoshop, Lightroom, Express and Firefly began a global rollout inside Gemini on September 24 . The "more than 50" figure is harder to place. PPC Land reported on August 12 that Google's own availability help article already listed 41 connected apps before that day's batch of 13 named partners, five of which were already on the list. Fourteen more followed in September. On October 13, Google said the Gemini app connects to "more than 40 apps" . Today's post counts Search and Gemini together. It does not say whether an app available in both products is counted once or twice, and the arithmetic from Google's earlier lists points to a total for Gemini alone that is already above 50. Google directs readers to its help center pages for Search and Gemini for the complete list. Several questions that matter to anyone weighing an integration go unanswered in the announcement. Economics. There is no mention of fees, revenue share or charges to developers, and nothing on whether users pay to reach any app beyond what the partner itself charges. Selection. When two ticketing apps or two fitness apps are both connected, which one does Search or Gemini call? The post does not describe how a request is routed, whether users must link an app before it can be used, or whether Google may suggest an app the user has not connected. For brands, that routing logic plays the role ranking plays in search results. Data. "Authenticated accounts" implies that users sign in to a partner service through Google, but the post does not describe the linking process, what user information passes from Google to the developer, what returns to Google, or how long either side keeps it. Connected apps change what an AI answer can do: instead of linking to a business, Search or Gemini can call the business's service directly. When Google first brought Instacart, Canva and YouTube Music into AI Mode in Search on July 16 , AI Mode assembled a task and then sent the user to the partner to finish it. Until now, which companies got that treatment was decided through partnerships announced in batches. A console with a submission queue turns it into something closer to an application process, even if Google keeps the final say through review. The audience on the Gemini side is large. Alphabet reported on July 22 that the Gemini app had reached 950 million monthly users . That app carries no advertising. Google's vice president of global ads, Dan Taylor, denied in December 2025 that ads were coming to Gemini , and in January said there were no plans for ads in the Gemini app . With no paid placement on offer, being a connected app is one of the few ways a brand can be present inside Gemini's interface at the moment a user asks for something it sells. The single build for two surfaces also fits what Google's leadership has been saying in public. Sundar Pichai, speaking on the Sources podcast on October 21, said agents rather than a merger of products would unify Search and Gemini . A developer registering once and switching on either product, or both, is that idea expressed as tooling. Measurement remains the gap. The console's metrics - traffic, latency and error rates - tell an engineering team whether the integration works. Neither the post nor the console view Google published shows any link to Google Ads, Google Analytics or conversion tracking. Brand control gets one line. Verified logos and authenticated accounts address a real risk in an open submission system: an app that looks like a well-known brand but is not. On October 15, Google began rolling out Universal Cart across US Search and the Gemini app , a cross-retailer basket that hands checkout to Google Pay or the merchant's site. Google today opened a preview of its Connected Apps Platform, a single route for outside developers to build their services into both Google Search and the Gemini app. The announcement, posted on Google's blog by Chips Mistry, Group Product Manager for Search, and Mai Lowe, Group Product Manager for the Gemini app, introduces a Google Connected Console where developers register, test and submit apps for review, and choose which of the two products each app appears in. Google also said it has now launched more than 50 Connected Apps across Search and Gemini, naming Adobe, Calm, Experian, Localiza and Peloton among its partners. Access is opening in phases, and the post gives no fees, no list of markets and no account of how Google decides which app handles a request.

Google is letting more companies build their apps into Google Search and the Gemini assistant, so people can do things like book a table or plan a workout without leaving Google. That matters to any business with an app, because these connected apps are the ones Search and Gemini can hand a task to when someone asks for help. For now it is a preview that opens in stages, and Google has not said what it costs, how it picks between competing apps, or what user data changes hands.

The post is short. Dated October 28, 2026, carrying a three-minute read time and filed under Developer tools, Search and Gemini App, it runs to five paragraphs under the headline "Build and manage Connected Apps in one place." Two announcements share the space: a developer platform, and a new set of consumer integrations.

On the first, the wording is direct. "To help users get more done, today we're launching the preview of our Connected Apps Platform, a unified way for more app developers to bring their capabilities directly into Gemini and Search," according to the post. Google frames the platform as a consolidation, describing it in the summary line as "a single place to build and manage apps for Search and the Gemini app."

The operative word is preview. "We're opening access in phases, and will add more developers, markets, and Google products over the coming months," the post states, pointing developers to a sign-up and documentation at developers.google.com/connected-apps. The announcement does not say how many developers are admitted in the first phase, which countries or languages are covered, or when the preview ends. The reference to adding "Google products" in the plural suggests the platform is meant to reach beyond Search and Gemini at some point, though the post names no other product.

The technical description fits in a single sentence. "Developers integrate with a cloud-hosted MCP server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, then use the Google Connected Console to register, test, and submit their app," according to Google.

Both routes rest on the Model Context Protocol , the open standard Anthropic introduced in November 2024 for connecting AI models to outside tools and data. An MCP server publishes a list of "tools" - discrete actions such as searching inventory, checking availability or placing a booking - which an AI model can call on a user's behalf. Google's platform accepts that standard rather than asking developers to adopt a proprietary format, which in principle lets a company reuse a server it already runs for other AI assistants.
That sequence places Google as a gatekeeper. Nothing goes live without review, though the developer, not Google, decides the publishing moment once approval is granted.

One decision is made before review. "Before review, developers choose whether it will go live in Search, the Gemini app, or both," according to the post. The pitch to developers is that a single build covers both. The platform, Google says, "gives developers the opportunity to build once and reach high-intent users across both Search and the Gemini app." No figure accompanies "high-intent," and the post does not say how many people use Connected Apps today.

After launch, the reporting is operational. "Once live, you can track traffic, latency, and error rates, and keep control of your brand identity, including verified logos and authenticated accounts," the post states. Traffic, latency and error rates are the measures an engineering team watches to keep a service running. The post mentions no conversion data, no revenue reporting and no visibility into which user requests triggered an app.

The second half of the post concerns the apps users can reach. "We've launched more than 50 Connected Apps between Search and Gemini in areas ranging from productivity and event ticketing to health and fitness," according to Google.

Four partners are singled out. "Integrations with partners like Adobe, Experian, Localiza, and Peloton are live for users in Gemini, and in the coming weeks, we'll be bringing these Connected Apps to Search as well," the post states. Localiza is a Brazilian car rental company; the post does not describe what its integration does or in which markets it is available. The fifth name is new across both products: "Among other apps, we'll also be launching a new integration with Calm across both Search and Gemini."

For three of the four Gemini names, the news today is Search. Adobe, Experian and Peloton were among the 14 connected apps Google began rolling out in Gemini on September 23 , a batch that also included Airtable, Linear, monday.com, Squarespace and Webflow. Adobe's tools from Photoshop, Lightroom, Express and Firefly began a global rollout inside Gemini on September 24 .

The "more than 50" figure is harder to place. PPC Land reported on August 12 that Google's own availability help article already listed 41 connected apps before that day's batch of 13 named partners, five of which were already on the list. Fourteen more followed in September. On October 13, Google said the Gemini app connects to "more than 40 apps" . Today's post counts Search and Gemini together. It does not say whether an app available in both products is counted once or twice, and the arithmetic from Google's earlier lists points to a total for Gemini alone that is already above 50. Google directs readers to its help center pages for Search and Gemini for the complete list.
Several questions that matter to anyone weighing an integration go unanswered in the announcement.
Economics. There is no mention of fees, revenue share or charges to developers, and nothing on whether users pay to reach any app beyond what the partner itself charges.

Selection. When two ticketing apps or two fitness apps are both connected, which one does Search or Gemini call? The post does not describe how a request is routed, whether users must link an app before it can be used, or whether Google may suggest an app the user has not connected. For brands, that routing logic plays the role ranking plays in search results.

Data. "Authenticated accounts" implies that users sign in to a partner service through Google, but the post does not describe the linking process, what user information passes from Google to the developer, what returns to Google, or how long either side keeps it.

Connected apps change what an AI answer can do: instead of linking to a business, Search or Gemini can call the business's service directly. When Google first brought Instacart, Canva and YouTube Music into AI Mode in Search on July 16 , AI Mode assembled a task and then sent the user to the partner to finish it. A console with a submission queue turns it into something closer to an application process, even if Google keeps the final say through review.

The audience on the Gemini side is large. Alphabet reported on July 22 that the Gemini app had reached 950 million monthly users . That app carries no advertising. Google's vice president of global ads, Dan Taylor, denied in December 2025 that ads were coming to Gemini , and in January said there were no plans for ads in the Gemini app . With no paid placement on offer, being a connected app is one of the few ways a brand can be present inside Gemini's interface at the moment a user asks for something it sells.

Neither the post nor the console view Google published shows any link to Google Ads, Google Analytics or conversion tracking.

Brand control gets one line. Verified logos and authenticated accounts address a real risk in an open submission system: an app that looks like a well-known brand but is not. The post does not say how verification works or what proof a developer must provide.

sources.title: Google expands AI Search ads globally as core ad growth slows
passages: Google is bringing ads in its AI-powered Search experiences to international markets, betting that generative AI can open up new revenue opportunities even as growth in its core search advertising business slows.
Google Search revenue grew 12% year over year in the third quarter, down from 17% growth in the second quarter and 19% in the first quarter.
The slowdown puts added pressure on Google to turn its expanding AI features into a meaningful source of advertising revenue.
The results follow a busy quarter for Google, including the release of Gemini 4 Argon , the growth of the Gemini app to one billion monthly users , and the launch of its Pixel 11 lineup .
Queries in AI Mode are three times longer on average than traditional searches, Pichai said, while one in five AI Mode searches globally involves voice, images, or documents.
Google has also surpassed 50 billion visual searches per month.
“This includes taking our monetization footprint global for the first time.
But Search advertising growth continued to decelerate, and Alphabet shares fell 8% following the results.
Google says early results suggest the formats are working.
The company’s user research also indicates that people find the ads relevant.

The move builds on Google’s May announcement of new Gemini-powered ad formats, including conversational discovery ads that respond to users’ questions and sponsored recommendations integrated into AI-generated answers.

extraction.body: Facebook-parent Meta is expected to overtake Alphabet’s Google in net digital advertising revenue this year, a report claims. If this prediction becomes true, it will mark a major shift in the global ad market. According to a report from research firm eMarketer shared with the Wall Street Journal (WSJ), Meta is expected to generate more than $243.46 billion in net ad revenue, slightly more than Google's projected $239.54 billion. These estimates take into account revenue after costs for acquiring traffic and creating content, such as the money Google pays to creators and partners. The expected change is due to a mix of product strategy, AI-driven improvements, and changing user behaviour, which have helped Meta grow its advertising base, the report claims. On the other hand, Google is growing more slowly and facing more competition in its core segments. Meta’s rise is being driven in part by its investment in newer formats and platforms, including Reels, Threads, and WhatsApp, where the company focused first on building user engagement before introducing ads. According to Max Willens, a principal analyst at Emarketer, Meta has demonstrated “incredible patience” in establishing user habits across these services before monetising them.How AI, Reels, and platform strategy is powering Meta’s ad growthAccording to Emarketer, Meta's advertising growth is expected to rise from 22.1% in 2025 to 24.1% this year, even though analysts expected it to slow due to the company's size. On the other hand, Google's global ad growth is expected to remain at 11.9%.A key contributor has been Meta’s use of artificial intelligence to improve content recommendations and ad delivery. The company said its AI recommendation systems increased Reels watch time in the US by more than 30% year over year in the most recent quarter, enabling it to show more ads. Reels alone is expected to generate $50 billion over the next 12 months, the WSJ reported.AI is also influencing how advertisers create campaigns. extraction.body: Facebook-parent Meta is expected to overtake Alphabet’s Google in net digital advertising revenue this year, a report claims. If this prediction becomes true, it will mark a major shift in the global ad market. According to a report from research firm eMarketer shared with the Wall Street Journal (WSJ), Meta is expected to generate more than $243.46 billion in net ad revenue, slightly more than Google's projected $239.54 billion. These estimates take into account revenue after costs for acquiring traffic and creating content, such as the money Google pays to creators and partners. The expected change is due to a mix of product strategy, AI-driven improvements, and changing user behaviour, which have helped Meta grow its advertising base, the report claims. On the other hand, Google is growing more slowly and facing more competition in its core segments. Meta’s rise is being driven in part by its investment in newer formats and platforms, including Reels, Threads, and WhatsApp, where the company focused first on building user engagement before introducing ads. According to Max Willens, a principal analyst at Emarketer, Meta has demonstrated “incredible patience” in establishing user habits across these services before monetising them.How AI, Reels, and platform strategy is powering Meta’s ad growthAccording to Emarketer, Meta's advertising growth is expected to rise from 22.1% in 2025 to 24.1% this year, even though analysts expected it to slow due to the company's size. On the other hand, Google's global ad growth is expected to remain at 11.9%.A key contributor has been Meta’s use of artificial intelligence to improve content recommendations and ad delivery. The company said its AI recommendation systems increased Reels watch time in the US by more than 30% year over year in the most recent quarter, enabling it to show more ads. Reels alone is expected to generate $50 billion over the next 12 months, the WSJ reported.AI is also influencing how advertisers create campaigns. Meta said the revenue run rate of its video-generation tools reached $10 billion in the fourth quarter, reflecting increased adoption of automated ad creation tools across its platforms. However, this expansion is accompanied by significant spending, with Meta’s capital expenditure expected to reach $135 billion this year.Google faces slower growth and rising competitionGoogle’s advertising business, which includes search, YouTube, and its network of partner sites, remains a major force but is facing pressure on multiple fronts. Competition from companies like Amazon is affecting search behaviour, as more users begin product searches directly on e-commerce platforms rather than traditional search engines.This year, Emarketer says that Google's share of the US search ad market will drop to 48.5%. This is the first time in more than ten years that it has dropped below 50%. At the same time, new competitors such as AI-powered platforms like OpenAI and social media sites like TikTok are likely to further change how people find information online.Google's varied ways of making money also make it harder for ads to grow. YouTube Premium and similar services make money through subscriptions, but they also reduce the number of people who see ads, limiting how much revenue ads can generate. Despite the projected leadership shift, the broader digital advertising market remains concentrated among a small group of companies. Meta, Google, and Amazon are expected to increase their combined share of the global digital ad market to 62.3% this year, up from 59.9% last year, according to Emarketer. However, both Meta and Google declined to comment on the projections.The report says that Meta's current success is due to its strategy around AI, short-form video, and gradual monetisation. However, competition and changes in how users interact with digital platforms will continue to change the advertising landscape in the years to come.
